# qagents 0.2.0: the full documentation

> A small, explicit agent framework for Python, with QCloud as the first-class model provider.

Every documentation page, in the order of the site navigation. Each page starts with a line that gives its path and its URL.

---

<!-- page: index.md | ./ -->

# qagents

A small, explicit agent framework for Python. One loop, typed tools, durable sessions, and QCloud
as the first-class model provider, without being tied to it.

```python
from qagents import Agent, tool


@tool(read_only=True)
def get_weather(city: str) -> str:
    """Look up the current weather for a city."""
    return f"Sunny in {city}"


agent = Agent("qcloud:<model-id>", instructions="Be brief.", tools=[get_weather])
result = agent.run_sync("What is the weather in Athens?")
print(result.output)
```

!!! warning "Status: 0.2.0, alpha"
    The offline test suite passes, including the QCloud provider driven through the real
    `qcloud_ai` SDK. No request has been made against the live QCloud API yet. See
    [what is verified](design.md#what-is-verified).

## What you get

| You want | You write | Read more |
|---|---|---|
| An answer | `await agent.run("...")` or `agent.run_sync("...")` | [The loop](concepts/loop.md) |
| Tokens and tool activity as they happen | `async for event in agent.stream("...")` | [Streaming](concepts/streaming.md) |
| A tool | a typed Python function with `@tool` | [Tools](concepts/tools.md) |
| A typed answer | `Agent(..., output_type=Invoice)` | [Structured output](concepts/structured-output.md) |
| A conversation that survives restarts | `session=Session(SQLiteStore("agents.db"), id="user-42")` | [Sessions](concepts/sessions.md) |
| A human in the loop | `@tool(requires_approval=True)` and `agent.resume(...)` | [Permissions](concepts/permissions.md) |
| Hard stops | `Limits(max_turns=..., max_cost_usd=..., timeout_s=...)` | [The loop](concepts/loop.md#limits) |
| Your code inside the loop | subclass `Hooks` | [Hooks](concepts/hooks.md) |
| Several agents | `tools=[other_agent]` or `handoffs=[other_agent]` | [Several agents](concepts/multi-agent.md) |
| Another coding agent as a worker | `tools=[DevviAgent(workspace=repo).as_tool(timeout=1800)]` | [External agents](concepts/external-agents.md), [Devvi](integrations/devvi.md) |
| Any ACP agent | `ACPAgent(["node", ".../bin.js", "--acp"], workspace=...)` | [Any ACP agent](integrations/acp.md) |
| Your tools inside a coding agent | `tool_server(tools, ctx=ctx)`, `expose_tools=[...]` | [Serving tools over MCP](integrations/mcp-server.md) |
| A multi-step job that resumes | `Workflow(store, id=...)` | [Workflows](concepts/multi-agent.md#workflows) |
| Traces | `hooks=[OTelHooks()]` | [Tracing](concepts/hooks.md#tracing) |
| Tests without a model | `ScriptedModel([...])` | [Testing](testing.md) |
| Docs your coding agent can query | `python -m qagents.docs_mcp` (MCP) or `qagents docs search "..."` | [Docs for coding agents](coding-agents.md) |

## Why another framework

The 2026 research behind this project ([report, in Greek](research.md)) found that agent
frameworks converged on the same small kernel, and that their documented gaps repeat. qagents is
built around the gaps that matter for a private, OpenAI-compatible model platform:

- **Resume at the tool call, not at the node.** Graph frameworks checkpoint at step boundaries
  and re-run the whole step after a crash or an approval. qagents journals every message, tool
  start and tool result as it happens, so a finished tool call never runs twice.
- **Nothing hidden.** Every string the framework sends to a model is in one file,
  [`qagents.prompts`](reference/prompts.md), and `Hooks.before_model` sees the exact request.
- **Provider rules enforced early.** QCloud rejects unknown request fields; qagents rejects them
  when the agent is built, with the list of accepted fields.
- **No replay of billable requests.** A request the provider may already have processed is never
  sent again unless you opt in.
- **Control by code, outside the model.** Permissions are deterministic rules; a failing check
  refuses the call.
- **Coding agents under your rules.** A coding agent such as Devvi is driven over ACP as an
  external agent: its permission requests go through your `Permissions`, your limits stop it,
  and your journal records the call. MCP is used only to give it tools.
  See [External agents](concepts/external-agents.md).

## Layout

```text
agent.py        the Agent, the loop, RunStream
messages.py     provider-neutral messages
tools.py        @tool, Tool, Toolkit, RunContext
permissions.py  allow / ask / deny rules and approvals
hooks.py        hook points around the run, the model request and each tool call
session.py      the journal: Session, InMemoryStore, SQLiteStore
workflow.py     durable steps for multi-step and multi-agent jobs
multi.py        fan_out and route
runtime.py      AgentRuntime: background runs with leases and recovery
context.py      compaction of long conversations
tracing.py      OpenTelemetry spans
evals.py        datasets, evaluators and reports
prompts.py      every string the framework itself sends to a model
models/         QCloudModel, OpenAIChatModel, AnthropicModel, FallbackModel, test models
stores/         PostgresStore
toolkits/       file, shell, web, notes, clock, planning, ask_user and MCP tools
external/       external agents: other agent programs driven over a control protocol
integrations/   the ACP client, Devvi, the MCP tool server, AG-UI events, MLflow tracing
docs_mcp/       the docs MCP server and command line for coding agents
cli.py          the qagents command: chat, run, models, docs
```

# Getting started

## Install

Python 3.11 or newer.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mpvasilis/qagents.git
cd qagents
python -m venv .venv
.venv/Scripts/activate        # Windows; on Linux/macOS: source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

The QCloud provider uses the `qcloud-ai` SDK. Until it is published on PyPI, install it from
source:

```bash
pip install "git+https://github.com/qcloud-host/qcloud-python.git"
```

## See it run without a key

`examples/offline_tour.py` uses a scripted model, so it needs no network:

```bash
python examples/offline_tour.py
```

It shows a streamed tool loop, a pause for approval that is resumed by a different agent object,
and a handoff.

## Your first agent on QCloud

Set `QCLOUD_API_KEY`. Pick a model id from the catalog that lists the `tools` capability
(`client.models.list()` in the SDK, or the public catalog at
`https://platform.qcloud.host/api/public/models`).

```python
import asyncio
from qagents import Agent, tool


@tool(read_only=True)
def get_order(order_id: str) -> dict:
    """Look up an order by its id.

    Args:
        order_id: The order id, for example "A-1001".
    """
    return {"id": order_id, "status": "delivered", "total_eur": 42.5}


agent = Agent(
    "qcloud:<model-id>",
    instructions="You are a support assistant for an online shop. Be brief.",
    tools=[get_order],
)


async def main() -> None:
    result = await agent.run("Has order A-1001 arrived?")
    print(result.output)
    print(result.usage.total_tokens, result.usage.cost_usd)


asyncio.run(main())
```

`"qcloud:<model-id>"` builds a [`QCloudModel`](providers.md#qcloud). To share one SDK client per
process, build the model yourself:

```python
from qcloud_ai import AsyncQCloud
from qagents import Agent, QCloudModel

client = AsyncQCloud()  # reads QCLOUD_API_KEY
agent = Agent(QCloudModel("<model-id>", client=client))
```

## Stream the answer

```python
async for event in agent.stream("Has order A-1001 arrived?"):
    if event.type == "text_delta":
        print(event.text, end="", flush=True)
    elif event.type == "tool_call_finished":
        print(f"\n[{event.call.name} -> {event.result.content}]")
```

## Keep the conversation

```python
from qagents import Session, SQLiteStore

store = SQLiteStore("agents.db")
await agent.run("My name is Maria.", session=Session(store, id="user-42"))
await agent.run("What is my name?", session=Session(store, id="user-42"))
```

## Check the live platform

`examples/live_acceptance.py` runs a handful of small paid requests against the real API
(streaming, a tool loop, structured output, error mapping) under a spend cap:

```bash
python examples/live_acceptance.py --dry-run   # no key: shows the model and the worst-case cost
python examples/live_acceptance.py             # needs QCLOUD_API_KEY
```

It reads the key from `QCLOUD_API_KEY`, a `.env` file next to `pyproject.toml`, or your Windows
user environment variables, and never prints it.

## Next

- [The loop](concepts/loop.md): what happens in a run, limits and stop reasons.
- [Tools](concepts/tools.md): schemas, context, errors and flags.
- [Sessions and recovery](concepts/sessions.md): what is guaranteed after a crash.

<!-- page: concepts/loop.md | concepts/loop/ -->

# The loop

An agent is a model, instructions and tools, run in a loop until the model answers.

## One rule decides the next step

Before every step the loop looks at the last message of the conversation:

| Last message | Next step |
|---|---|
| assistant message with tool calls that have no results | run the tools |
| assistant message without tool calls | that is the final answer |
| anything else (a user message, tool results) | ask the model |

The next step depends only on the conversation, and the conversation is written to the
[session journal](sessions.md) as it grows. That is why a run can stop anywhere and continue
later: the loop that resumes is the same loop, reading the same history.

```
run_started
  turn 1:  model request  ->  assistant message (maybe with tool calls)
           tool calls     ->  tool results
  turn 2:  model request  ->  assistant message
run_finished
```

## What a run returns

`agent.run()` returns a [`RunResult`](../reference/events.md). Check `status` before `output`:

| `status` | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `completed` | The agent answered. `output` is the text, or the validated `output_type` value. | Use it. |
| `paused` | Tool calls in `pending_approvals` wait for a decision. | [`agent.resume`](permissions.md#pause-and-resume) |
| `limit_reached` | A limit stopped the run; `stop_reason` names it. | Report it, or continue with a new `run` on the session. |
| `cancelled` | `RunStream.cancel()` was called. | Continue with a new `run` on the session. |

Failures are exceptions, not statuses: a provider error after retries (`ModelError`), a hook that
raised, or a final answer that never matched `output_type` (`OutputValidationError`). The session
keeps everything that happened before the failure, so `agent.resume(session)` continues the run.

`result.messages` is the whole conversation, `result.new_messages` only what this run added,
`result.usage` the tokens and cost, and `result.session` the session to pass to the next call.

## Limits

Every run has hard stops. The defaults are deliberately not "unlimited".

```python
from qagents import Agent, Limits

agent = Agent(
    "qcloud:<model-id>",
    limits=Limits(max_turns=12, max_total_tokens=200_000, max_cost_usd=0.50, timeout_s=300),
)
result = await agent.run("...", limits=Limits(max_turns=3))  # per-run override
```

| Limit | Default | Checked |
|---|---|---|
| `max_turns` | 30 | before each model request |
| `max_total_tokens` | off | before each model request |
| `max_cost_usd` | off | before each model request; needs a model that reports cost |
| `timeout_s` | off | continuously: cancels the request or tool in flight |
| `tool_timeout_s` | 120 | per tool call, unless the tool sets its own `timeout` |
| `output_retries` | 2 | extra attempts when the answer does not match `output_type` |
| `model_retries` | 2 | extra attempts for model errors that are safe to repeat |

A run stopped by a limit has `status == "limit_reached"` and `stop_reason` set to `max_turns`,
`max_total_tokens`, `max_cost_usd` or `timeout`. Its history is still valid. To let it go on,
start a run on the same session without a prompt and with a higher limit:

```python
result = await agent.run("Research the topic", session=session, limits=Limits(max_turns=5))
if result.stop_reason == "max_turns":
    result = await agent.run(session=session, limits=Limits(max_turns=20))
```

## Retries and billing

Model errors carry two flags. `retryable` means the request could succeed if sent again.
`ambiguous` means the provider may already have processed, and billed, the request: a timeout
after sending, a dropped connection, a 5xx, a stream that ended early.

The loop repeats a request only when it is `retryable` and not `ambiguous` (a 429 is the typical
case), and never after part of the answer was already streamed to you. To also repeat ambiguous
requests, set `Limits(retry_ambiguous=True)` and accept the possible double charge.

## Instructions

`instructions` is fixed text, or a function of the run context:

```python
async def instructions(ctx: RunContext[Deps]) -> str:
    return f"You are helping {ctx.deps.user_name}. Today is {ctx.deps.today}."


agent = Agent("qcloud:<model-id>", instructions=instructions)
await agent.run("...", deps=Deps(user_name="Maria", today="2026-11-11"))
```

The instructions are sent as the system message of every request and are not stored in the
conversation, so each agent in a [handoff](multi-agent.md#handoffs) applies its own.

## Settings

`ModelSettings` holds sampling and tool-choice settings; unset fields are not sent.

```python
from qagents import ModelSettings

agent = Agent("qcloud:<model-id>", settings=ModelSettings(temperature=0.2, max_tokens=800))
await agent.run("...", settings=ModelSettings(max_tokens=200))  # merged over the agent's
```

`ModelSettings(extra={...})` passes provider-specific request fields as they are. QCloud
publishes an allow-list, so an unknown field fails when the agent is built.

---

<!-- page: concepts/tools.md | concepts/tools/ -->

# Tools

A tool is a Python function the model can call. Decorate it with `@tool`.

```python
from typing import Literal
from qagents import tool


@tool(read_only=True)
async def search_orders(customer: str, status: Literal["open", "closed"] = "open") -> list[dict]:
    """Find a customer's orders.

    Args:
        customer: Customer email.
        status: Which orders to return.
    """
    return [{"id": "A-1001", "status": status, "customer": customer}]
```

## What the model sees

The signature becomes a JSON Schema and the docstring becomes the description. For the function
above the model receives:

```json
{
  "name": "search_orders",
  "description": "Find a customer's orders.",
  "parameters": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "customer": {"type": "string", "description": "Customer email."},
      "status": {"type": "string", "enum": ["open", "closed"], "default": "open",
                 "description": "Which orders to return."}
    },
    "required": ["customer"],
    "additionalProperties": false
  }
}
```

Inspect it with `search_orders.spec`. Parameters can be anything pydantic understands, including
nested models. `*args` and `**kwargs` are rejected, because they cannot be described to a model.
Sync functions run on a worker thread; async functions run on the event loop.

Write descriptions for the model: say what the tool does, when to use it, and what each argument
means. That text is most of what the model knows about your system.

## The run context

A first parameter annotated `RunContext` (or named `ctx`) is filled in by the loop and hidden
from the model.

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass
from qagents import Agent, RunContext, tool


@dataclass
class Deps:
    db: "Database"
    user_id: str


@tool(read_only=True)
async def my_orders(ctx: RunContext[Deps]) -> list[dict]:
    """List the current user's orders."""
    return await ctx.deps.db.orders(ctx.deps.user_id)


agent = Agent("qcloud:<model-id>", tools=[my_orders])
await agent.run("What did I order?", deps=Deps(db=db, user_id="u-42"))
```

| Field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `deps` | whatever you passed as `deps=`: connections, the current user, configuration |
| `state` | JSON state shared between tool calls, persisted in the session journal across runs and resumes; tools that change it must use `read_only=False` |
| `run_id`, `session_id`, `agent_name`, `turn` | where the call is happening |
| `tool_call_id` | the model's id for this call |
| `operation_id` | a stable id for this call: [use it as an idempotency key](sessions.md#idempotency) |
| `usage`, `messages` | snapshots of the run so far |
| `emit(event)` | put a custom event on the run's stream |
| `add_usage(usage)` | count model usage your tool caused in the run total |

## Results and errors

Whatever the function returns is rendered to text for the model: strings as they are, everything
else as JSON, `None` as `OK`. Long results are shortened in the middle
(`Limits.max_tool_result_chars`, default 60,000 characters).

Mistakes go back to the model as error results, so it can correct itself:

| Situation | What the model reads |
|---|---|
| unknown tool name | `There is no tool named 'x'. Available tools: ...` |
| arguments are not valid JSON | a request to call again with a valid JSON object |
| arguments fail validation | the failing fields and messages |
| your tool raises `ToolError("...")` | your message |
| your tool raises anything else | `'x' failed: <Type>: <message>` (also logged with a traceback) |
| the tool exceeds its timeout | `'x' did not finish within N seconds and was stopped.` |

Raise `ToolError` when the model can do something about the failure, and write the message for
the model: what went wrong and what to try instead.

```python
from qagents import ToolError


@tool
def refund(order_id: str, amount: float) -> str:
    """Refund an order."""
    if amount > 100:
        raise ToolError("Refunds above 100 EUR need a human. Tell the customer you escalated it.")
    return f"Refunded {amount:.2f} EUR."
```

## Flags

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `@tool(read_only=True)` | changes nothing: may run in parallel with other read-only calls |
| `@tool(requires_approval=True)` | asks a human first, unless a permission rule allows it |
| `@tool(idempotent=True)` | safe to repeat after a crash |
| `@tool(timeout=10)` | seconds; overrides `Limits.tool_timeout_s` |
| `@tool(name="lookup", description="...")` | override what is derived from the function |

**Parallelism.** When the model requests several tools in one turn, calls to `read_only` tools
run concurrently and all other calls run one at a time, in the order the model wrote them. This
keeps two writers from racing. Change it with `Limits(parallel_tools="all")` or `"none"`.

## Toolkits

A list of tools is already a toolkit: `tools=[file_tools("./workspace"), get_order]` flattens
nested lists. For tools that are only known at run time, subclass `Toolkit`:

```python
from qagents import Tool, Toolkit


class TenantTools(Toolkit):
    def __init__(self, tenant: str) -> None:
        self.tenant = tenant

    async def tools(self) -> list[Tool]:
        return await load_tools_for(self.tenant)
```

`tools()` is called when a run starts. See [ready-made tools](../toolkits.md) for the bundled
ones.

---

<!-- page: concepts/permissions.md | concepts/permissions/ -->

# Permissions and approvals

Whether a tool call runs is decided by ordinary code, outside the model. A prompt cannot talk its
way past a rule.

## The decision order

For every tool call the loop asks `Permissions.decide`, which checks in this order and stops at
the first match:

1. `deny` patterns: the call is refused.
2. `can_use_tool`: your function may allow, ask or deny, or return `None` for "no opinion".
3. `ask` patterns: a human is asked.
4. `allow` patterns: the call runs.
5. The `mode` default.

The first rule that answers decides. `deny` is checked first, so a deny always wins; an allow
from `can_use_tool` skips the `ask` rules, `requires_approval` and the mode. If anything goes wrong
while deciding (your callback raises, or returns something that is not a decision), the call is
refused.

```python
from qagents import Agent, Permissions

agent = Agent(
    "qcloud:<model-id>",
    tools=[read_order, refund_order, send_email, delete_customer],
    permissions=Permissions(
        allow=["read_*"],
        ask=["send_*", "refund_*"],
        deny=["delete_*"],
    ),
)
```

Patterns are shell-style and match tool names.

| `mode` | Calls that no rule matched |
|---|---|
| `"default"` | tools declared `requires_approval=True` ask; the rest run |
| `"allow_all"` | run |
| `"ask_all"` | ask |
| `"read_only"` | run only if the tool is declared `read_only=True`; otherwise refused |

A refused call is not an exception. The model receives an error result such as
`'delete_customer' was not run: a deny rule matches this tool.` and can tell the user.

## Decisions that depend on the arguments

```python
def refunds_up_to_20(ctx, tool, call):
    if tool.name == "refund_order":
        return "allow" if call.arguments["amount"] <= 20 else "ask"
    return None  # no opinion: continue with the rules


permissions = Permissions(can_use_tool=refunds_up_to_20)
```

`can_use_tool` may be async, and may return `"allow"`, `"ask"`, `"deny"`, a bool, a `Decision`
with a reason, or `None`.

## Approvals, inline

When the answer is "ask" and you gave an `on_ask` handler, it is awaited on the spot. Use this
where a person is present: a terminal, a chat UI holding a connection open, a Slack button.

```python
from qagents import Approval, Permissions


async def ask_in_slack(ctx, tool, call, reason) -> Approval:
    approved = await slack.confirm(f"Allow {tool.name}({call.arguments})?")
    return Approval(approved=approved, reason=None if approved else "Declined in Slack.")


permissions = Permissions(on_ask=ask_in_slack)
```

An `Approval` can also carry `arguments`, to run the tool with values the approver edited. If the
handler raises, the call is refused.

## Pause and resume

Without `on_ask`, the run pauses. Nothing is held in memory: the pause is written to the session,
so the approval can arrive minutes or days later, in another process.

```python
result = await agent.run("Refund order A-1001", session=session)

if result.status == "paused":
    for pending in result.pending_approvals:
        print(pending.tool_call_id, pending.name, pending.arguments, pending.reason)

    result = await agent.resume(
        session,
        approvals={result.pending_approvals[0].tool_call_id: True},
    )
```

`approvals` maps tool call ids to `True`, `False` or an `Approval`. What to know:

- Calls of the same turn that needed no approval ran before the pause. They are not run again.
- Approve only some of the pending calls and the run pauses again with the rest.
- A declined call becomes an error result with your reason, and the model continues from it.
- If you did not pass a session, one was created: use `result.session`.
- The pending calls are also in `(await session.state()).pending_approvals`, which is what an
  approvals page would read.

### Signed pauses

Configure `Permissions(approval_secret=...)` to sign paused approvals and deferred inputs.
Return `Approval.for_call(pending)` or `InputResult.for_call(pending, value)` when resuming;
these carry the recorded token. A missing token or a changed signed call raises
`ApprovalTokenError` before a tool runs. Authenticate whoever calls `resume` in your
application: the token protects the paused call's integrity, not the reviewer's identity
or the rest of the journal.

Signed JSON integers must be between `-(2**53 - 1)` and `2**53 - 1`, inclusive. Larger
integers are refused rather than rounded. PostgreSQL JSONB can normalize an integral float
to an integer; a large float normalized outside this range also fails verification on
resume. Use strings for identifiers or exact quantities beyond the safe integer range.

---

<!-- page: concepts/sessions.md | concepts/sessions/ -->

# Sessions and recovery

A session is a conversation that outlives a process.

```python
from qagents import Agent, Session, SQLiteStore

store = SQLiteStore("agents.db")
session = Session(store, id="user-42")

await agent.run("My name is Maria.", session=session)
await agent.run("What is my name?", session=session)  # sees the first exchange
```

`Session()` alone keeps the conversation in memory. A store and an id make it durable. The id is
yours to choose; include the tenant and the user in it when your application has several.

## The journal

A session is an append-only journal of JSON entries. The loop writes an entry for every message,
every tool start and every tool result at the moment it happens.

| Entry | Written when |
|---|---|
| `run_started` | a run begins |
| `message` | a message joins the conversation |
| `tool_started` | a tool call begins executing |
| `tool_result` | a tool call has a result |
| `agent_switched` | a handoff changes the active agent |
| `run_paused` | the run stops to wait for approvals |
| `run_finished` | the run ends (`completed`, `limit_reached`, `cancelled`, `abandoned`) |
| `run_failed` | the run raised; it stays open and can be resumed |
| `compaction` | the history sent to the model was replaced by a shorter one |
| `workflow_step` | a workflow step finished |

The current state is derived by reading the journal: `await session.state()` returns the
messages, the open run if there is one, recorded tool results and pending approvals. Nothing is
pickled, and nothing depends on the shape of your code, so a run can be resumed by a different
process, after a deploy, or after the agent's tools changed.

```python
for entry in await session.entries():
    print(entry.seq, entry.kind, entry.run_id)
```

## Resuming

`agent.resume(session)` continues the session's unfinished run: after a
[pause for approval](permissions.md#pause-and-resume), a crash, or a provider error.

```python
state = await session.state()
if state.open_run_id is not None:
    result = await agent.resume(session)
```

### What is guaranteed

Stated plainly, because the details matter when tools have side effects:

- **A tool call with a recorded result never runs again.** Its result is read from the journal.
- **A tool call that had started when the process died** has an unknown outcome. It is re-run
  only if the tool is declared `read_only` or `idempotent`. Otherwise the model is told that the
  outcome is unknown and that it should check before repeating.
- **A tool call that had not started** runs normally, after the usual permission check.
- **A model request that was in flight** is sent again. Its first response was lost, so this
  costs tokens, but no tool had acted on it. The model's response is always journaled before any
  tool it requested starts.
- **Delivery is at-least-once**, as in every agent framework. Exactly-once needs cooperation from
  the system your tool calls: see below.

`agent.resume` continues a run; nothing calls it for you. Finding dead runs across replicas
(leases, heartbeats, a recovery worker) is on the [roadmap](../design.md#roadmap). Until then,
resume from your own job runner or on the user's next request.

### Idempotency

Every tool call has `ctx.operation_id`. It is the same when the call is repeated after a resume,
and different for every other call. Pass it to the system the tool talks to:

```python
@tool(idempotent=True)
async def charge_card(ctx: RunContext[Deps], amount_cents: int) -> str:
    """Charge the customer's saved card."""
    charge = await ctx.deps.payments.charge(
        amount=amount_cents,
        idempotency_key=ctx.operation_id,  # a repeat returns the first charge
    )
    return f"Charged, receipt {charge.receipt}"
```

Declaring the tool `idempotent=True` is your promise that a repeat is safe; with the key above it
is.

### A new message while tool calls are open

If the user sends a new message while a run is paused or was interrupted, `agent.run` closes the
open tool calls with a result that says they were not run (or that their outcome is unknown), and
marks the old run `abandoned`. The conversation stays valid for the provider, and the model knows
what did not happen.

## Stores

| Store | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `InMemoryStore` | tests, and sessions that need not survive a restart |
| `SQLiteStore(path)` | one host; WAL mode, calls run on worker threads |
| `PostgresStore(dsn)` | sessions shared by workers on several hosts; install `qagents[postgres]` |

A basic store implements three methods. A custom backend can implement this interface:

```python
from qagents.session import Entry, SessionStore


class MyStore(SessionStore):
    async def append(self, session_id: str, entries: list[Entry]) -> None:
        """Durably add entries to the end of the session, in order."""

    async def load(self, session_id: str) -> list[Entry]:
        """Return every entry of the session, oldest first."""

    async def delete(self, session_id: str) -> None:
        """Remove the session."""
```

`append` must be atomic and must preserve order. Entries are plain JSON (`entry.model_dump()`).

The built-in stores also support leases for runtime workers; a custom store needs the lease
methods to support `AgentRuntime`. `PostgresStore` opens a connection pool on first use
and keeps its tables in a separate schema.

!!! note "Journal snapshots"
    State is derived by reading the whole session journal. Long-lived sessions with thousands
    of entries will want snapshots, which are not implemented yet.

---

<!-- page: concepts/streaming.md | concepts/streaming/ -->

# Streaming and cancel

`agent.stream()` starts a run and returns a `RunStream`: an async iterator of events, plus
control over the run.

```python
stream = agent.stream("Tell me about Athens")
async for event in stream:
    if event.type == "text_delta":
        print(event.text, end="", flush=True)
result = stream.result  # the same RunResult agent.run() returns
```

For the answer text only, use `stream.text()`:

```python
async for piece in agent.stream("Tell me about Athens").text():
    print(piece, end="", flush=True)
```

## Events

Every event is a pydantic model with a `type` field.

| `type` | When | Useful fields |
|---|---|---|
| `run_started` | the run begins | `run_id`, `session_id`, `agent`, `resumed` |
| `turn_started` | a model request is about to be sent | `turn`, `agent` |
| `text_delta` | the model wrote some answer text | `text` |
| `reasoning_delta` | the model exposed some reasoning | `text` |
| `tool_call_delta` | the model is writing a tool call | `index`, `name`, `arguments_delta` |
| `model_responded` | one model response is complete | `response` (message, usage, finish reason) |
| `tool_call_started` | a tool begins executing | `call` |
| `tool_call_finished` | a tool call has a result: ran, failed, refused or cancelled | `call`, `result`, `duration_ms` |
| `approval_required` | a tool call waits for a human | `approval` |
| `agent_switched` | a handoff changed the active agent | `from_agent`, `to_agent` |
| `subagent_event` | an event from an agent running as a tool | `agent`, `tool_call_id`, `event` |
| `run_finished` | always last, unless the run raised | `result` |

Events serialise to JSON as they are, which makes forwarding them to a browser a one-liner:

```python
async for event in agent.stream(prompt, session=session):
    await websocket.send_text(event.model_dump_json())
```

See [serving over HTTP](../serving.md) for a complete server-sent-events endpoint.

`Hooks.on_event` receives the same events, for logging or metrics without consuming the stream.

## Cancel

```python
stream = agent.stream("Write a long story")
async for event in stream:
    if user_pressed_stop():
        stream.cancel()  # keep iterating: run_finished still arrives
print(stream.result.status)  # "cancelled"
```

`cancel()` stops the run at the next chunk or tool boundary:

- The connection to the model is closed, which makes QCloud abort the upstream request.
- The text produced so far is kept in the conversation as an assistant message with
  `metadata == {"interrupted": True}`.
- Tool calls that were running are cancelled and get a result saying so, so the history stays
  valid. A read-only call is reported as cancelled (`TOOL_CANCELLED`). Any other call, an
  idempotent one included, may already have changed things, so its outcome is reported as
  unknown (`TOOL_INTERRUPTED`) and the model is told to check before calling it again.
- The next `agent.run` on that session continues from the interrupted answer.

`Limits(timeout_s=...)` uses the same mechanism and ends the run as `limit_reached` with
`stop_reason == "timeout"`.

## Real-time and voice

For a voice agent the path above is the barge-in path: when the user starts speaking, call
`stream.cancel("barge_in")`, then start a new run with what they said. The model already knows
what it managed to say, because the partial answer is in the history.

What qagents gives a real-time pipeline: token-level streaming with no buffering in the loop,
cancellation that reaches the provider, and time to first token measurable from `turn_started`
to the first `text_delta`. What it does not include: speech-to-text, text-to-speech, audio
transports, and turn detection. Those belong to your media stack.

Two things to keep off the hot path: approvals that wait for a human (use permission rules that
decide immediately), and slow `before_model` hooks.

---

<!-- page: concepts/structured-output.md | concepts/structured-output/ -->

# Structured output

Give the agent an `output_type` and `result.output` is a validated value instead of text.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel
from qagents import Agent


class Invoice(BaseModel):
    number: str
    total: float
    currency: str = "EUR"


agent = Agent("qcloud:<model-id>", instructions="Extract invoices.", output_type=Invoice)
result = await agent.run("Invoice INV-7 for 120 euros")
invoice: Invoice = result.output
```

`output_type` can be a pydantic model, a dataclass, a `TypedDict`, or any type pydantic can
validate, such as `list[Invoice]`.

## How it works

The agent can still call tools first. When the model stops calling tools, its last message is
taken as the answer, parsed as JSON and validated:

1. The JSON is read tolerantly: bare JSON, JSON in a code fence, or JSON with a few words around
   it are all accepted.
2. It is validated against `output_type`.
3. On failure the model receives the validation error and tries again, up to
   `Limits.output_retries` times (default 2). After that, `OutputValidationError` is raised.

## Two modes

| `output_mode` | What is sent | Use it when |
|---|---|---|
| `"native"` (default) | the schema as `response_format: {"type": "json_schema", ...}` | the model or server enforces JSON schemas |
| `"prompted"` | the schema appended to the instructions | the model has no schema support |

```python
agent = Agent("qcloud:<model-id>", output_type=Invoice, output_mode="prompted")
```

The appended text is `qagents.prompts.OUTPUT_INSTRUCTIONS`; you can read and replace it.

A schema constraint guarantees shape, not correctness, so validation and retries run in both
modes. `output_strict=True` sets `strict` on the schema for providers that support strict mode;
they then require every property to be listed as required and `additionalProperties: false`.

!!! note "Model support varies"
    Whether a given catalog model honours `response_format` depends on the model and on how it
    is served. Run `examples/live_acceptance.py` against the model you plan to use; it includes a
    structured-output check. If it fails there, use `output_mode="prompted"`.

---

<!-- page: concepts/multi-agent.md | concepts/multi-agent/ -->

# Several agents and workflows

There are three ways to combine qagents agents, and a fourth for another agent program. Pick by
who should control the flow.

| Pattern | Who decides what happens next | Context |
|---|---|---|
| [Sub-agent](#sub-agents) | the calling agent's model | the sub-agent starts fresh and returns one answer |
| [Handoff](#handoffs) | the current agent's model, once | the next agent continues the same conversation |
| [Workflow](#workflows) | your code | each agent step has its own session |
| [External agent](external-agents.md) | the calling agent's model | another agent program with its own context, tools and model; returns its final message and a footer |

There are no role-play crews or group chats. The published evidence favours one orchestrator with
isolated workers and a single writer; see the [research report](../research.md).

## Sub-agents

Pass an agent in another agent's `tools`. It becomes a tool with one argument, `task`.

```python
researcher = Agent(
    "qcloud:<model-id>",
    name="researcher",
    description="Finds facts in the knowledge base and cites them.",
    instructions="Research thoroughly. Answer with facts and sources only.",
    tools=[search],
)
lead = Agent("qcloud:<model-id>", name="lead", tools=[researcher])
result = await lead.run("How fast did solar grow in 2025?")
```

- The sub-agent sees only the task text, not the caller's conversation. The tool description
  tells the calling model to make the task self-contained.
- The caller sees only the sub-agent's final answer, so long tool output stays out of its context.
- The sub-agent's usage is added to the caller's `result.usage`.
- Its events arrive on the caller's stream as `subagent_event`.
- If the sub-agent stops early (a limit, a pause), the caller's model gets an error result.

`agent.as_tool(name=..., description=..., read_only=True)` gives you the tool explicitly, for
example to let several read-only sub-agents run in parallel.

!!! note "Limits and approvals of sub-agents"
    A sub-agent cannot pause the caller for approval. Give sub-agents permission rules that
    decide immediately, or an `on_ask` handler; a child whose permissions have none uses the
    caller's `on_ask`, and the caller's hooks with `propagate = True` run in it too. A child's
    token, cost and time budgets are capped at what remains of the caller's, and children that
    run at once share it live. Runs nest at most `Limits.max_depth` levels (5 by default, the
    lowest value along the chain applies); a deeper child is not started, and the caller's
    model gets `prompts.SUBAGENT_TOO_DEEP`.

## Handoffs

A handoff transfers the conversation to another agent, which answers the user directly.

```python
billing = Agent(
    "qcloud:<model-id>",
    name="billing",
    description="Handles invoices, payments and refunds.",
    instructions="You are the billing specialist.",
    tools=[get_invoice, issue_refund],
)
triage = Agent(
    "qcloud:<model-id>",
    name="triage",
    instructions="Route the customer to the right specialist.",
    handoffs=[billing],
)
result = await triage.run("How much is my invoice?", session=session)
print(result.agent)  # "billing"
```

The triage model sees a tool named `transfer_to_billing`. When it calls it, the billing agent's
model, instructions, tools and `output_type` take over, on the same history. `result.agent` names
the agent that was active when the run stopped; a later `agent.resume(session)` continues with
that agent.

The agent you called `run` on still owns the run's `limits`, `permissions` and `hooks`. For the
next user message, call `run` on whichever agent should start: `billing.run(...)` to stay with
the specialist, `triage.run(...)` to route again.

## Workflows

When your code should decide the order, write a normal async function and wrap each unit of work
in a `Workflow` step.

```python
from qagents import Workflow


async def weekly_report(topic: str, store) -> str:
    wf = Workflow(store, id=f"report:{topic}:2026-W46")
    notes = await wf.run_agent("research", researcher, f"Research {topic}")
    draft = await wf.run_agent("write", writer, f"Write a report from these notes:\n{notes.text}")
    await wf.run_agent("publish", publisher, draft.text)
    return draft.text
```

External changes belong in durable agent tools. Pass `ctx.operation_id` to a service that
enforces an idempotency key; set `idempotent=True` only with that guarantee. Otherwise keep
the tool non-idempotent and reconcile an unknown outcome before trying again. An unfinished
plain `Workflow.step` may execute again after a crash.


- `wf.step(name, function)` records a pure or read-only function's result. When the same workflow
  id runs again, a finished step returns the recorded result; an unfinished function may repeat.
- `wf.run_agent(name, agent, prompt)` runs an agent in its own durable session. If the step was
  interrupted, the agent run is resumed at the exact tool call rather than restarted.
- Results must be JSON-serialisable. Pass `type=` to get a recorded value back as a model:
  `await wf.step("fetch", fetch, type=Report)`.
- Step names are the durable identity of the work. Do not rename them while runs are in flight,
  and make them unique (`f"summarise-{index}"` in a loop).

Parallel branches are plain asyncio. No branch waits for a slower one:

```python
import asyncio

europe, asia = await asyncio.gather(
    wf.run_agent("research-europe", researcher, "Research the EU market"),
    wf.run_agent("research-asia", researcher, "Research the Asian market"),
)
```

Approvals inside a workflow: a paused agent step is returned as it is and is not recorded as
finished. Call the same step again with the decisions to continue it.

```python
result = await wf.run_agent("send", mailer, "Send the newsletter")
if result.status == "paused":
    decisions = {p.tool_call_id: True for p in result.pending_approvals}
    result = await wf.run_agent("send", mailer, "Send the newsletter", approvals=decisions)
```

What is guaranteed: a step that finished never runs again. A plain `step` that was in progress
when the process died runs again from its start, so make side-effecting steps idempotent.

---

<!-- page: concepts/external-agents.md | concepts/external-agents/ -->

# External agents

A coding agent such as Devvi runs its own loop, with its own model, tools and sandbox. qagents
can put one to work: give it a task in a workspace, follow what it does, decide every permission
request it sends, stop it, and read its answer. Such an agent is an **external agent**.

| Thing | What it is | Who runs the loop | Who runs the tools |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Model` | one request in, one response out | qagents | qagents |
| `Agent` | a qagents loop over a `Model` | qagents | qagents |
| `ExternalAgent` | another agent program, reached over a control protocol | the external agent | the external agent; qagents decides every permission request it sends |

An external agent is not a model. Wrapping a coding agent as a `Model` would hide its tool calls
from the qagents journal and its permission requests from your rules. So qagents talks to it as
an agent, through `qagents.external.ExternalAgent`. Two adapters ship:

- [`ACPAgent`](../integrations/acp.md) drives any agent that speaks ACP v1, the Agent Client
  Protocol.
- [`DevviAgent`](../integrations/devvi.md) drives Devvi, over ACP (the default) or over Devvi's
  own SDK protocol.

## Two planes: who drives the agent, and what tools it has

Two different protocols are in play, and they point in opposite directions.

```text
 CONTROL PLANE: who drives the agent. ACP v1 or the Devvi SDK, JSON-RPC over the agent's stdio.

 +---------------------------+   task, session, cancel, answers   +------------------------+
 | qagents                   | ---------------------------------> | coding agent           |
 |   your lead Agent         |                                    |   Devvi, any ACP agent |
 |   coder = DevviAgent(...) | <--------------------------------- |   own loop and model,  |
 |   tools=[coder.as_tool()] |   text per step, tool calls,       |   own tools, sandbox   |
 +---------------------------+   permission requests, turn end    +------------------------+
                                                                              |
 TOOL PLANE: what tools the agent can call. MCP.                              | MCP tool calls
 The agent is the MCP client; qagents serves the tools.                       v
                                                       +-------------------------------------+
                                                       | qagents MCP tool server             |
                                                       |   your qagents tools, decided by    |
                                                       |   your Permissions, journaled in    |
                                                       |   your run                          |
                                                       +-------------------------------------+
```

**The control plane drives the agent.** qagents is the client and the agent is the server. The
client opens a session in a workspace, sends a task, receives the agent's steps as they are
committed, answers its permission requests, and can cancel the turn while keeping the session.
ACP is the standard protocol for this, and Devvi also has its own SDK protocol. Both are
JSON-RPC 2.0 over the agent's standard input and output.

**The tool plane gives the agent tools.** Here the agent is the client. MCP, the Model Context
Protocol, lets an agent list a server's tools and call them. qagents can serve its own tools
over MCP to an agent it drives ([Serving tools over MCP](../integrations/mcp-server.md)).

!!! warning "There is no MCP for driving a coding agent"
    MCP is a tool protocol. One MCP tool call is one request and one result. A coding agent's
    turn is something else: a session in a workspace, many steps, permission requests that
    come back to the caller in the middle of the turn, and a cancel that stops the turn but
    keeps the session. MCP is not built for that; ACP is.

    - **Devvi has no MCP server.** It ships an MCP client only (`packages/mcp/mcp-client`;
      paths like this one on this page name files in the Devvi repository); the MCP server
      SDK appears only in that package's development dependencies
      (`packages/mcp/mcp-client/package.json`). There is nothing for an MCP client to connect
      to.
    - **`MCPToolkit` cannot drive Devvi or any coding agent.** `qagents.toolkits.mcp.MCPToolkit`
      gives a qagents agent the tools of an MCP server. An agent that serves itself as an MCP
      tool (Codex: `codex mcp-server`) can be sent a task that way, but MCPToolkit cannot
      follow its steps, answer its permission requests or cancel it.
    - Even where an agent can be wrapped as a single MCP tool, the whole turn is then one
      opaque call: qagents could not see its steps, decide its permission requests one by one,
      or cancel the turn and keep the session.

    To make a coding agent work for you, use `ACPAgent` or `DevviAgent`. To give that agent
    your tools, serve them over MCP. The two combine: qagents drives Devvi over ACP and hands
    it qagents tools over MCP in the same session (`DevviAgent(expose_tools=[...])`).

Which piece to use for which job:

| You want | Use | Protocol | Who is the client |
|---|---|---|---|
| A coding agent does work for your qagents agent | `DevviAgent`, `ACPAgent`, then `.as_tool()` | ACP v1 or the Devvi SDK | qagents |
| Your qagents agent calls the tools of an MCP server | `qagents.toolkits.mcp.MCPToolkit` | MCP | qagents |
| A coding agent calls your qagents tools | `tool_server(...)`, or `DevviAgent(expose_tools=[...])` | MCP | the coding agent |
| A coding agent reads the qagents docs | `python -m qagents.docs_mcp` ([Docs for coding agents](../coding-agents.md)) | MCP | the coding agent |

## Using an external agent

The usual shape is a lead agent that plans and reviews, with a coding agent as one of its tools.

```python
from qagents import Agent, Limits, Permissions
from qagents.integrations.devvi import DevviAgent

coder = DevviAgent(
    workspace="C:/work/repo",
    patches=[{"id": "tool-web", "disabled": True}],  # Devvi without its web tools
    allow_unmetered=True,  # ACP reports no token counts; the cost cap then counts the lead only
)
lead = Agent(
    "qcloud:<model-id>",
    instructions="Plan the change, delegate the code edits to `coder`, then review them.",
    tools=[coder.as_tool(name="coder", timeout=1800)],
    permissions=Permissions(
        ask=["coder.bash", "coder.pwsh"],  # Devvi asks only to leave its sandbox
        deny=["coder.web_fetch"],  # defense in depth: Devvi does not ask before a web fetch
    ),
    limits=Limits(max_cost_usd=2.0, timeout_s=3600),
)

async with coder:
    result = await lead.run("Make tests/test_parser.py pass.")
```

The lead's model sees one tool, `coder(task, session=None)`. Each call is one turn of the
external agent, run as a child of the lead's tool call:

- it starts at depth + 1 and is refused beyond `Limits.max_depth`;
- its events reach the lead's stream as `subagent_event`;
- the permission requests it sends are decided by the lead's `Permissions`, on names such as
  `coder.bash`, with the lead's `on_ask`; Devvi sends one only for a step that asks to leave its
  sandbox (see [below](#what-qagents-decides-and-what-the-agent-decides));
- cancelling the lead, or the lead's timeout, cancels the turn;
- its token usage, when the agent reports any, is added to the lead's run as it arrives. In a
  tool of your own that runs `result = await coder.run(task, parent=ctx)`, the usage is already
  counted, so `ctx.add_usage(result.usage)` adds nothing, as for an `Agent` child.

The lead's model reads the agent's final message and a footer that qagents adds. Here the coder
read a file, ran the tests without asking, then asked to run a command outside its sandbox;
an `ask` rule matched, and with no `on_ask` the request was refused:

```text
Fixed parse_line; the test passes.

[coder: session coder-1; completed; 3 tool calls (pwsh 2, read 1); 1 permission refused (pwsh: "Remove-Item -Recurse C:/build")]
```

To continue the same conversation, the model passes `session` from the footer in its next call.
It can continue only a session that this tool opened in this qagents session (the latest 50
are kept in `ctx.state["qagents.external.sessions"]`). Any other session id is a tool error
that says so (`coder failed: session ... was not opened by coder in this conversation; leave
session out to start a new one`), and the agent is not reached. Once the list holds 50 sessions,
the refusal uses `EXTERNAL_AGENT_FORGOTTEN_SESSION`: `session ... is not among the last 50
sessions that coder opened or continued in this conversation, which are the only ones it can
continue; leave session out to start a new one`. The session may have been dropped from the
list even if this tool opened it earlier. Your own code may continue any session:
`coder.run(task, session=...)` and `coder.stream(task, session=...)`.
Give `as_tool()` a `timeout` that fits coding work: without one the lead's
`Limits.tool_timeout_s` applies, which is 120 seconds by default, and the turn is cancelled at
about 110 seconds ([Budgets, limits and cancel](#budgets-limits-and-cancel)).

You can also run a turn directly and follow its events:

```python
async with coder:
    async with coder.stream("Add type hints to utils.py") as turn:
        async for event in turn:
            print(event.type)
    print(turn.result.status, turn.result.changed_files)
```

`coder.run(task)` does the same and returns the `ExternalResult`. The result is a pydantic model,
so a `Workflow` step can record it; see [Devvi as a worker](../integrations/devvi.md#as-a-workflow-step).

## What qagents decides, and what the agent decides

| qagents decides | The external agent decides |
|---|---|
| Whether the agent runs at all: `as_tool(requires_approval=True)`, the depth limit, a budget it cannot report against | Which tools it has and what they do (`read`, `edit`, `bash`, ...) |
| The answer to every permission request the agent sends, through your `Permissions` | When to ask: qagents sees only the requests the agent chooses to send |
| Time: `as_tool(timeout=...)`, `Limits.tool_timeout_s`, `Limits.timeout_s` of the calling run | Its sandbox: what a command may touch without asking |
| Tokens and cost, when the agent reports usage | Its model, its system prompt, its context management |
| Steps per turn: `max_external_turns` (50 by default) | How it plans and when it is done |
| Cancelling a turn, and killing the process tree when it does not stop | Its own session log, the full inner transcript |
| What the calling run journals, and whether a call is repeated after a crash | |
| The process: its command, working directory and environment variables | |
| Which qagents tools it gets, and the rules for each call it makes to them | |

Two consequences matter.

**A tool call the agent does not ask about runs without a qagents decision.** You see it as a
`tool_call_started` event while it runs, not before, and no rule of yours is consulted. Devvi
allows a tool call unless one of its gates says "ask"
(`packages/core/tools/src/pipeline.ts`). With its default profile only an
escalation asks: a shell command or file change sent with `sandbox_permissions` (for example
`"danger-full-access"` in Devvi's recorded transcript
`snapshots/acp/escalation-approved/stdout.expected.jsonl`). Measured in tier 1
under the default `workspace-write` mode: file writes and ordinary commands inside the
workspace, web fetches and MCP tool calls ran with no request, even with a deny rule on
`coder.web_fetch` (`test_a_web_fetch_runs_without_a_permission_request` in
`tests/integrations/test_integration_docs.py`). So a rule on `coder.web_fetch` or `coder.read`
is never consulted: to take a tool away, remove it from the agent itself, for Devvi with a patch
row ([Devvi permissions](../integrations/devvi.md#permissions)).

**The agent's sandbox is the agent's, not qagents'.** Devvi's sandbox modes govern file effects
only; network and process policy are outside them
(`packages/sandbox/sandbox-policy/README.md`). On Windows its enforcement
is reported as `partial`: reads stay unconfined and NTFS hard links can alias files outside the
workspace (`packages/sandbox/sandbox-local/README.md`). Do not treat it as
a security boundary. For real isolation, run the agent in a disposable clone or a container, and
gate the delegation instead of each command (see
[the recipe](../integrations/devvi.md#gate-the-delegation-not-each-command)).

## Permission requests

Every permission request of the agent goes through a `PermissionBridge`. It asks the turn's
`Permissions` about a synthetic call named `"<prefix>.<agent tool>"`: the prefix is the tool
name the calling model sees (`coder`), or the agent's `name` for a direct run. The arguments
are those of the matching tool call. The synthetic tool is declared `requires_approval=True`,
so when no rule matches, the decision is "ask".

The rules are, in this order: `stream(permissions=...)`, the agent's own `permissions=`, the
calling run's. When the chosen rules have no `on_ask`, the calling run's `on_ask` is used.

| Decision | What the agent is answered |
|---|---|
| a deny rule, or `can_use_tool` refuses or raises | reject (`decided_by="rules"`): this one action is refused and the turn goes on |
| an allow rule, or the mode allows | allow this one call (`rules`) |
| ask, and `on_ask` approves | allow this one call (`on_ask`) |
| ask, and `on_ask` declines or raises | reject (`on_ask`) |
| ask, and `on_ask` approves with edited arguments | reject (`edited_arguments`): qagents cannot change what the agent runs |
| ask, no `on_ask` | depends on the posture, below |
| the decision took longer than `approval_timeout_s`, or failed outside your rules and `on_ask` | "cancelled" (`timeout`, `error`): the agent does not run the tool |
| the tool call's latest input is not a JSON object | "cancelled" (`unreadable_arguments`), without asking the rules: they cannot see what would run |
| a request that arrives, or a decision that ends, while the turn is being cancelled | "cancelled" (`cancelling`), also for an allow that came in at that moment |

An "allow always" option is never chosen, even when the agent offers one: every grant covers
one call. When the agent offers no "allow once" option, an allow is sent as "cancelled"
(`no_option`), and the record says so.

**Postures.** `on_permission=` on the agent chooses what "ask" without an `on_ask` does:

| Posture | Ask without `on_ask` | Default `approval_timeout_s` | Use it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"rules"` (default) | refused (`no_approver`); the refusal is in the result and in the footer | 60 s | rules decide everything; the lead's model reads the refusal and adapts |
| `"pause"` | the turn ends, and the calling run pauses until a human answers | 60 s | a person approves commands, possibly days later |
| `"live"` | refused, as `"rules"` | 900 s | an `on_ask` that waits for a person in a long-lived process |

### Pause for a human

With `on_permission="pause"`, a request that needs a human answers the agent "cancelled", ends
the external turn, and pauses the calling run with a `PendingInput` (reason `"permission"`). Its
`metadata` names the agent, the external session, the tool, the arguments and a fingerprint.
Answer it with `ExternalApproval`:

```python
from qagents import Agent, Session, SQLiteStore
from qagents.external import ExternalApproval
from qagents.integrations.devvi import DevviAgent

coder = DevviAgent(workspace="C:/work/repo", on_permission="pause", allow_unmetered=True)
lead = Agent("qcloud:<model-id>", tools=[coder.as_tool(name="coder", timeout=1800)])

async with coder, SQLiteStore("agents.db") as store:
    session = Session(store, id="fix-42")
    result = await lead.run("Clean the build folder, then run the tests.", session=session)
    if result.status == "paused":
        pending = result.pending_inputs[0]
        print(pending.metadata["tool"], pending.metadata["arguments"])  # coder.bash {...}
        answer = ExternalApproval.for_input(pending, approved=True)
        result = await lead.resume(session, results={pending.tool_call_id: answer})
```

The lead's model reads the answer as the result of its paused call, for example
`Approved: coder may run bash "rm -rf build" once. Call coder again with session=... to
continue.` When it calls `coder` again with that session, the agent is told the action was
decided (`EXTERNAL_AGENT_CONTINUE`), and the first request with the same fingerprint (the
prefixed tool name and the canonical JSON of the arguments) is allowed, once. Free text that
the agent writes anew on each attempt is left out of the fingerprint
(`ExternalAgent.grant_ignored_arguments`; for Devvi `description` and `justification`), so the
same command with a reworded description is still the approved request. If the agent asks
for something else, that request is decided afresh. Deny rules still refuse it whatever the
approval says. A direct run (no calling run to pause) refuses as `"rules"` does.

A tool built with `as_tool(continuable=False)` has no `session` parameter: its next call
continues the paused session by itself, and the approval text does not mention `session=`.

## Budgets, limits and cancel

| Trigger | What happens |
|---|---|
| The calling run is cancelled, or its `timeout_s` expires | the turn is cancelled; the call's result says its outcome is unknown (`TOOL_INTERRUPTED`), because the agent may have changed files before it stopped, and the session stays in `ctx.state["qagents.external.sessions"]` |
| `as_tool(timeout=T)` expires | the turn is cancelled with reason `timeout`; the model is told, with the session to continue |
| No `timeout`, and the calling run's `Limits.tool_timeout_s` is more than `2 × (cancel_grace_s + 5)` (20 s by default) | the turn is cancelled at `tool_timeout_s - (cancel_grace_s + 5)` seconds, so the cancel is graceful and the model is told the session |
| No `timeout`, and a shorter `Limits.tool_timeout_s` | the loop's own tool timeout ends the call at `tool_timeout_s`: the model reads `TOOL_TIMEOUT` (`'coder' did not finish within 3 seconds and was cancelled. ...`), without the session or the footer |
| The calling run's `max_total_tokens` or `max_cost_usd` is used up by the agent's reported usage | the turn is cancelled as `limit_reached` |
| The calling run has `max_total_tokens` or `max_cost_usd`, and the agent reports no token usage | the call is refused before a session or a turn starts, unless the agent was built with `allow_unmetered=True`. The agent process may already be running: the handshake comes first (for an ACP agent, the process starts and answers `initialize`) |
| More than `max_external_turns` steps (default 50) | the turn is stopped as `limit_reached` (`max_external_turns`) |
| The call would nest deeper than `Limits.max_depth` | refused before the agent starts |

A step is one model request where the protocol reports it (the Devvi SDK's `step/start`), and
one tool call where it does not (ACP).

**One turn at a time.** One turn runs at a time per workspace (across all the external agents
of the process) and per session; a call waits for that, and the `as_tool(timeout=...)` time
includes the wait. A call whose time runs out while it waits was never started: the model
reads `EXTERNAL_AGENT_BUSY`, and the footer says `no session; cancelled (busy)`. A turn
cancelled before it starts, or while it waits, ends at once (`raw["not_started"]`), without
starting the agent.

**Cancel.** qagents asks the agent to stop (ACP: `session/cancel`; the Devvi SDK has no
per-turn cancel, so the process is shut down). The agent then has `cancel_grace_s` seconds
(default 5) to end the turn. If it does not, the turn is abandoned, the whole process tree is
killed, and the result has `raw["forced"] = True`; the next turn starts a new process.

**Unmetered agents.** ACP carries no token counts, only context pressure. A calling run with a
token or cost budget therefore refuses an ACP agent, because the budget could not be enforced.
Build the agent with `allow_unmetered=True` to accept that its spend is not counted (the lead's
own spend still is). The refusal happens at the first call, not when the agent is built, and
after the handshake: the agent's process is started and stays up, but no session is opened and
no prompt is sent. To count Devvi's tokens and cost, use its SDK transport with prices
([Token usage and cost](../integrations/devvi.md#token-usage-and-cost)).

## The journal and crash recovery

The calling run journals an external call like any tool call: `tool_started` before it runs,
`tool_result` after, with the final text plus the footer as the content and the usage the
agent reported. The inner transcript is not copied into the calling conversation: the lead's
context stays small, and the journal does not depend on the agent's format. The agent's own
session log stays the record of what happened inside.

Besides that, qagents keeps:

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| `ctx.state["qagents.external.sessions"]` | per tool name, the sessions it used in this qagents session (`session_id`, `cwd`, `backend`; the last 50) |
| `ctx.state["qagents.external.grants"]` | pauses waiting for an answer (posture `"pause"`) |
| journal entries of kind `tool_checkpoint` | facts a resumable call records before it ends: the external session id (`external_session`), adapter facts such as "the prompt was sent" or Devvi's message id, and the finished result (`external_result`); readers that do not know the kind ignore it |

**After a crash.** When the process running the lead dies and the run is resumed:

- A call whose `tool_result` was journaled is not run again.
- A call that was running is repeated only when the agent's turns are resumable
  (`resumable_turns`). `DevviAgent` is resumable on both transports by default; `ACPAgent` only
  with `resumable=True`. The repeat re-attaches to the session the first attempt journaled:
  - if the first attempt had finished and only its `tool_result` was lost, the recorded result
    is returned and no turn runs;
  - otherwise the agent continues the same session and is told the previous attempt was
    interrupted (`EXTERNAL_AGENT_RESUME`: check the workspace state and finish the task);
  - on the Devvi SDK transport, a turn that Devvi's session log shows as finished is replayed
    from the log and not prompted again;
  - if the agent no longer has the journaled session, or cannot reopen it, the call ends
    `interrupted` with an unknown outcome and the task is not sent again
    (`ACP_NOT_REATTACHED`, `DEVVI_NOT_REATTACHED`): the earlier attempt may have sent it. The
    model is told to check the workspace and to call again without a session
    (`EXTERNAL_AGENT_INTERRUPTED_NO_SESSION`).
- A call to an agent that is not resumable is not repeated: the lead's model is told that its
  outcome is unknown, as for any interrupted tool with side effects.

### Guarantees for external calls

| Guarantee | Scope |
|---|---|
| A call whose result was journaled never runs again | always (the agent loop) |
| A call that was running when the process died is repeated only for a resumable agent, and the repeat continues the journaled session instead of starting a new one | `DevviAgent` (both transports, by default), `ACPAgent(resumable=True)` |
| A repeated call whose first attempt finished returns the recorded result without a new turn | resumable agents, once the result checkpoint was written |
| A repeated call does not prompt Devvi again when its session log shows the turn finished | Devvi SDK transport, with the default uncompressed log |
| Every permission request is decided by your rules, and never answered "allow always" | always |
| A permission check that raises (`can_use_tool`, `on_ask`) answers reject; a timeout or any other failure while deciding answers "cancelled"; either way the tool does not run | always |
| A turn whose connection broke is reported `interrupted`, with `raw["ambiguous"] = True`, and never counted as completed; a plain `error` only when the adapter knows nothing of the turn was sent | always |
| A repeated call whose session the agent no longer has (or cannot reopen) is not sent again | resumable agents |
| One turn at a time per workspace, and per continued session | within one process |
| The agent's reported usage counts against the caller's budgets as it arrives | agents that report usage (Devvi SDK) |

Not guaranteed:

- **Exactly-once work inside the agent.** A repeated call asks the agent to check the workspace
  and finish; it may redo part of the work. Use a git workspace and review the diff.
- **A decision before every tool call.** Only the calls the agent asks about are decided
  before they run.
- **Cost of agents that report no usage.** With `allow_unmetered=True` it is not counted.
- **Live tokens.** See below.
- **The agent's sandbox as a security boundary.**

## Text arrives per step, not per token

Devvi sends whole committed blocks: each `text_delta` holds a finished paragraph or message of
the agent, not a few tokens. Its ACP bridge derives updates from committed session events
(`packages/acp/acp/src/updates.ts`), and its ACP README says raw provider
deltas stay off the wire (`packages/acp/acp/README.md`). The SDK protocol
sends committed session events too (`session.event`,
`packages/sdk/protocol/src/types.ts`): a whole `assistant/message` per model
request. `ExternalCapabilities.live_tokens` is `False` for Devvi on both transports.

So a UI shows the coder's work step by step: a message, a tool call, its result, the next
message. Do not build a "typing" effect on it. An ACP agent that streams token chunks gets them
forwarded as it sends them; qagents does not merge or split text.

Committed blocks are separated by a blank line when the adapter tells blocks apart
(`text_delta(text, message_id=...)`): Devvi's blocks on both transports, and ACP chunks with a
new `messageId`. Two blocks with no tool call between them then read
`"Fixed it.\n\nTests pass."`, not `"Fixed it.Tests pass."`; the blank line is also at the
start of the second block's `text_delta`. Token chunks of one message are joined as they
arrive. A tool call starts a new message: the turn's final text is the text after the last
tool call.

## Events

A turn emits ordinary qagents events. A turn used as a tool reaches the caller's stream as
`SubagentEvent` (its `agent` is the tool name), which `RunStream` consumers, `Hooks.on_event`
and the AG-UI projection handle as for an agent used as a tool.

A direct turn (`agent.stream(...)`) is like a `RunStream`: it has `run_id`, `text()` (only the
text), `cancel()`, `wait()` and `aclose()`. But it ends with the `external_event`
`turn_finished`, not `run_finished`. `to_agui_events(turn)` ends the AG-UI run at that event:
`RUN_FINISHED` for `completed`, `cancelled` and `limit_reached`, `RUN_ERROR` for `error` and
`interrupted`. The agent works in its own process
whether or not you read the events, so use a direct turn in `async with`, or read it to the
end: breaking out of `async for` cancels the turn.

| Event | When |
|---|---|
| `run_started` | the session is known (`run_id` is `ext:<session>:<12 hex>`, unique for every turn; an `as_tool()` call keeps its id when the calling run repeats it after a crash; `resumed` says whether the session was continued) |
| `turn_started` | a model request of the agent starts (Devvi SDK only) |
| `text_delta`, `reasoning_delta` | the agent committed a message or a thought |
| `model_responded` | a model response with usage (Devvi SDK only) |
| `tool_call_started`, `tool_call_finished` | a tool call of the agent, named `<prefix>.<tool>`; qagents measures the duration |
| `external_event` | anything without a qagents counterpart; `kind` says what |

`ExternalAgentEvent` (`type="external_event"`) kinds:

| `kind` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `permission_requested`, `permission_decided` | every permission request and its answer (`tool`, `arguments`, `outcome`, `rule`, `decision`, `reason`) |
| `tool_arguments` | a started tool call got new input: `{tool_call_id, name, arguments}`. On ACP every `tool_call_update` with new `rawInput` emits one, so expect it often. The `tool_call_started` event keeps the first arguments; `tool_call_finished` carries the latest |
| `approval_refused` | Devvi SDK: a request about a call its session never started, answered "cancelled" without consulting your rules (`{toolName, callId, reason: "unknown_call"}`) |
| `context` | ACP context pressure, `{used, size}`; not token usage |
| `config` | the agent changed a session option |
| `plan` | an ACP plan update |
| `image`, `audio` | the agent sent an image or audio (`mimeType` only; the bytes are not forwarded) |
| `resource_link`, `resource` | ACP: the agent sent a link to a resource (`name`, `uri`, `mimeType`) or an embedded resource (`uri`, `mimeType`; not its content) |
| `retry`, `compaction`, `job`, `attempt` | Devvi SDK: a model retry, a context compaction (its usage is counted), a background job, an abandoned attempt |
| `web_search` | Devvi SDK: the DeepSeek web search made a model request of its own, which Devvi records without usage; qagents counts it as one request whose tokens and cost are unknown (`usage.unpriced_requests`) |
| `approval_asked`, `approval_decided` | Devvi SDK: Devvi's own audit records of a request that qagents also reports as `permission_*` |
| `subagent_started`, `subagent_finished` | Devvi SDK: one of Devvi's own subagents started (`parent_session_id`, `depth`) or finished (`status`, `stopReason`, a short `text`); `session_id` is the subagent's |
| `subagent_event` | Devvi SDK: a step of one of Devvi's own subagents |
| `unknown`, `raw` | unmapped updates, only with `raw_events=True`; otherwise they are counted in `ExternalResult.raw["ignored_events"]` |
| `turn_finished` | always the last event: status, stop reason, session, backend, usage, tool call counts, permissions, changed files (`changed_files`: the first 100 paths; `changed_files_count`: all of them; `ExternalResult.changed_files` has every path) |

## What the calling model reads

The tool is `name(task, session=None)` (`continuable=False` drops `session`). Its description is
the agent's `description`, or a default that tells the model the agent sees only the task text.

A completed turn returns the final text and the footer. Anything else is an error result whose
footer names the session when the turn had one. A turn that never began in a session (it was
refused, it waited too long for its workspace, or it broke before the agent confirmed one)
names no session, also when the call asked to continue one: `[coder: no session; cancelled
(busy)]`.

| Status | The calling model reads |
|---|---|
| `completed` | the final text, then `[name: session ...; completed; N tool calls (...); refused requests; changed: files]` |
| `cancelled`, `limit_reached` | `coder stopped before finishing (timeout).`, the text so far, the footer |
| `error` | `coder failed: <the agent's message>`, the footer |
| `error` that will repeat (authentication, billing, a missing credential), or a setup failure | `coder is unavailable: ... do not call coder again`; later calls in the same run fail at once |
| `interrupted` (the process exited, a pipe broke) | `coder stopped unexpectedly (...) ... Its outcome is unknown: check what it changed before calling it again.`, with the session to continue |
| `interrupted` with no session (it broke before one was opened, or a repeated call's session is gone) | `coder stopped unexpectedly (...) before it had a session it can continue. ... To try again, call it without a session.` |
| refused before the start | `coder was not started: ...` (too deep, or an unmetered agent under a budget) |

Every one of these strings, and the few the ACP and Devvi adapters add, is a plain module
attribute in [`qagents.prompts`](../reference/prompts.md). Nothing else is added to what the
models read.

`ExternalResult` holds the same facts as data: `status`, `stop_reason`, `text`, `session_id`,
`backend` (for example `devvi-acp@0.2.1-rc.3`), `usage`, `tool_calls`, `permissions`,
`changed_files` (with git tracking, by default when the workspace is a git repository), and
`raw`. `await result.diff()` gives the `git diff` of the changed files on demand; qagents never
sends it to a model.

Through `as_tool()` the same facts reach the tool result: `ToolResultPart.metadata["external"]`
has `status`, `stop_reason`, `session_id`, `backend`, `usage`, `tool_calls` (counts per name),
`permissions`, `changed_files` (the first 100) and `changed_files_count`, and
`metadata["ambiguous"]` is `True` when the turn was interrupted and its outcome is unknown.

The agent can write the repository's `.git/config`, so git runs with a small environment (no
secrets, no network transport) and with every program that config could name switched off:
fsmonitor, filters, an external diff, textconv and the pager. Submodules' work trees are not
looked into. git itself is found on `PATH`, never in the workspace or the current directory.

`stop_reason` uses one vocabulary for every agent: `end_turn`, `max_tokens`, `cancelled`,
`content_filter` and the limit names (`STOP_REASONS` in `qagents.external`). An `error` turn's
`stop_reason` is the agent's message, and a word an adapter cannot map passes through. The
agent's own word stays in `raw`: `raw["acp_stop_reason"]` for an ACP agent,
`raw["agent_stop_reason"]` for Devvi on both transports.

## Testing offline with `ScriptedExternalAgent`

`ScriptedExternalAgent` plays scripted turns in memory, the way `ScriptedModel` plays model
replies. Everything else is the real code: the permission bridge, the footer, the events,
budgets and the journal.

```python
from qagents import Agent, Permissions
from qagents.external import ScriptedExternalAgent, ToolStep
from qagents.messages import Usage
from qagents.models.testing import ScriptedModel, call


ESCALATION = {
    "command": "Remove-Item -Recurse C:/build",
    "sandbox_permissions": "danger-full-access",  # Devvi asks only for steps like this one
}


async def test_the_lead_delegates_and_an_escalation_is_refused():
    coder = ScriptedExternalAgent(
        [
            [  # one turn of the coder
                "Reading the parser.",
                ToolStep("read", {"path": "src/parser.py"}, result="def parse_line..."),
                ToolStep("pwsh", {"command": "pytest -q"}, result="1 passed"),  # not asked
                ToolStep("pwsh", ESCALATION, ask=True),  # asked: it wants to leave the sandbox
                Usage(requests=1, input_tokens=120, output_tokens=40),
                "Fixed parse_line; the test passes.",
            ]
        ],
        name="coder",
    )
    model = ScriptedModel([call("coder", task="Fix parse_line and run the test."), "Done."])
    lead = Agent(model, tools=[coder.as_tool()], permissions=Permissions(ask=["coder.pwsh"]))

    result = await lead.run("Fix the parser.")

    assert result.output == "Done."
    assert [(a.outcome, a.decided_by) for a in coder.answers] == [("deny", "no_approver")]
    footer = model.requests[1].messages[-1].tool_results[0].content
    assert "1 permission refused (pwsh" in footer
```

Only the step with `ask=True` reaches the rules, as with a real agent: the first `pwsh` call
runs without a decision although an `ask` rule matches its name.

A turn is a list of steps:

| Step | Plays |
|---|---|
| `"text"` | a committed message (`text_delta`); two in a row are separated by a blank line |
| `ReasoningStep(text)` | a thought |
| `ToolStep(name, arguments, result="OK", is_error=False, ask=False)` | a tool call; with `ask=True` the agent asks first and runs the tool only when allowed |
| `PermissionStep(name, arguments, reason=None)` | a permission request without a tool call |
| `EventStep(kind, data)` | an `external_event` |
| `Usage(...)` | reported token usage (added to the calling run at once) |
| `WaitStep(seconds=None, ignore_cancel=False)` | wait, or until cancelled; `ignore_cancel=True` plays an agent that does not stop |
| `EndStep(status, stop_reason, text)` | end the turn with that status |
| an exception instance | raised; an `ExternalAgentConnectionError` plays a crashed process |
| a function of the `ExternalTurnContext` | anything else, sync or async |

The agent records what it received: `calls` (task, session, cwd, `resumed`, checkpoints,
answers), `prompts`, `answers` (every `PermissionAnswer`), `connects`, `disconnects` and
`cancel_requests`. New sessions are named `"<name>-<n>"`. By default it reports token usage
and is not resumable, unlike `DevviAgent` on ACP: pass `capabilities=ExternalCapabilities()`
to test an unmetered agent, and `resumable_turns=True` to test crash re-attach. To stand in for
`DevviAgent` in a test of your lead, set both
([Test your lead offline](../integrations/devvi.md#test-your-lead-offline)).

To test an adapter against a real process without the real agent, the test suite has fake
peers (`tests/integrations/fakes/fake_acp_agent.py` replays recorded ACP transcripts); see
[Adding a recorded fixture](../integrations/acp.md#adding-a-recorded-fixture-for-a-new-agent).

## Writing an adapter

Subclass `qagents.external.ExternalAgent` and implement `capabilities()` and
`run_turn(turn)`; optionally `connect()`, `disconnect()` and `cancel_turn(turn)`. `run_turn`
reports everything through the `ExternalTurnContext` it receives (`begin`, `text_delta`,
`tool_started`, `tool_finished`, `add_usage`, `ask_permission`, ...) and returns an
`ExternalOutcome`. Raise `ExternalAgentConnectionError` when the connection broke: the turn
