  not report its token usage`). With this setting a coder built without `allow_unmetered=True`
  fails the test the same way. For `transport="sdk"` with `pricing=`, keep the default and add
  `Usage(...)` steps.
- **`resumable_turns=True`**: as `DevviAgent`, whose `resumable` is on by default. The tool is
  then idempotent, so a call that was running when the lead's process died is repeated on
  resume and re-attaches to its session. With the default (`False`) the lead's model is told
  the outcome is unknown instead.

Only steps with `ask=True` reach the lead's rules, as with Devvi, which asks only for
escalations ([Permissions](#permissions)). On Linux and macOS Devvi's shell tool is `bash`.

## Running the tests

On Windows PowerShell, from the qagents checkout:

```powershell
pytest tests/integrations -q                      # tier 0: offline, no Devvi, always
$env:QAGENTS_DEVVI_BIN = "C:\src\devvi-harness\apps\cli\lib\bin.js"
pytest -m devvi_mock tests/integrations -q        # tier 1: real Devvi, local mock model, opt-in
python examples/devvi_coder.py --workspace C:\tmp\devvi-sandbox --dry-run
python examples/devvi_coder.py --workspace C:\tmp\devvi-sandbox --lead qcloud:<model-id>
```

Tier 0 replays Devvi's own recorded transcripts (copied into `tests/fixtures/devvi/`, with
Devvi's MIT notice) through fake peers that the tests start as real processes. Tests marked
`devvi_mock` are skipped unless `-m` names the marker (`tests/integrations/conftest.py`).

Tier 1 (`tests/integrations/test_devvi_mock.py`, plus the `devvi_mock` tests in
`tests/integrations/test_integration_docs.py` that check this page's claims) runs the real
Devvi CLI against a local mock of the model API (`tests/integrations/mock_model_server.py`,
ported from Devvi's own `scripts/smoke-python-runtime.py`), so it needs no key and
costs nothing. It needs `QAGENTS_DEVVI_BIN` (the tests skip without it); `QAGENTS_NODE` and
`QAGENTS_DEVVI_TMP` (where each test's own Devvi home and workspace go) are optional. Every test
starts one or two Devvi processes, 3 to 10 seconds each on Windows. With a Node older than
24.9.0 the tests start Devvi through `tests/integrations/devvi_node_compat.mjs`, a module hook
for `import.meta.main`, and warn that they do.

A tier 2 against a paid model route is planned: the conftest registers a `devvi_live` marker,
but no test uses it yet.

## What is verified

| Area | How |
|---|---|
| ACP transport: handshake, sessions, model options, permissions, cancel, re-attach after a crash, one process per workspace, pause posture | offline tests against Devvi's recorded ACP transcripts and a fake `devvi` process |
| SDK transport: event mapping, usage and cost, approvals, cancel by shutdown, re-attach from the session log | offline tests against Devvi's recorded SDK snapshots and a fake Devvi home |
| Launcher: CLI and Node discovery, `.cmd` shims, versions, home, environment allowlist, patch checks | offline tests |
| `expose_tools` | offline tests with the official MCP client |
| The example | `--dry-run`, offline |
| The real Devvi CLI, both transports: the doctor's handshakes, a text turn, a shell tool that writes in the workspace, escalations decided by qagents rules, cancel during a tool, resuming a session from a second agent, SDK usage and cost, SDK crash recovery from the session log | tier 1 (`-m devvi_mock`) |
| What Devvi asks about: ordinary commands and web fetches run without a request under `workspace-write`; only escalations are asked; the `tool-web` patch row removes the web tools | tier 1: `test_acp_escalation_is_decided_by_qagents_rules`, `test_a_web_fetch_runs_without_a_permission_request`, `test_a_disabled_tool_web_row_removes_devvis_web_tools` |
| The file sandbox follows the session's `cwd`, not the process's | tier 1: `test_acp_the_file_sandbox_follows_the_session_cwd_not_the_process_cwd` |
| `expose_tools` with the real Devvi: its MCP client takes the bearer header and the `127.0.0.1` URL; Devvi's model calls the tool; Devvi asks no permission for it; two turns of one session, closed after each and resumed with a new server; the calls are journaled in the lead's session | tier 1: `test_acp_exposed_qagents_tools_are_called_by_devvis_model_over_mcp` |
| SDK: `session/prompt` for a stored session that was not resumed is refused (-32603 `session "<id>" already exists`): no new session, no fork | tier 1: `test_sdk_a_prompt_for_a_stored_session_that_was_not_resumed_is_refused` |
| SDK: a session of another workspace is refused before Devvi opens it | tier 1: `test_sdk_a_session_of_another_workspace_is_refused` |
| A missing `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` fails closed on both transports, without a model call | tier 1: `test_a_missing_api_key_fails_closed` |

The tier 1 results above come from Devvi 0.2.1-rc.3 on Windows 11 with Node 22.17, started
through `tests/integrations/devvi_node_compat.mjs`. Re-run tier 1 on Node 24.9 or newer, where
the tests start Devvi without the hook, before you rely on them for your setup. On that machine
the two `workspace-write` shell tests were expected failures (xfail) because of the sandbox ACLs
in [Windows notes](#windows-notes).

Not covered by any test against a running Devvi: QCloud as Devvi's model route; a paid model
route (tier 2); Linux and macOS; Node 24.9 or newer without the compatibility hook.

## Not in this version

- **Authentication is never automatic.** qagents starts no login for Devvi. Give Devvi's model
  route its key through the environment (`env_passthrough`, by variable name). Headless model
  authentication for Devvi is planned for later.
- The devvi.sh platform's model endpoint as a qagents `Model` (a `DevviPlatformModel`).
- qagents as an ACP agent server, so that ACP clients could drive a qagents agent.
- Tests against a paid model route (tier 2): the `devvi_live` marker exists, no test uses it
  yet.

---

<!-- page: integrations/acp.md | integrations/acp/ -->

# Any ACP agent

The [Agent Client Protocol](https://agentclientprotocol.com) (ACP) is how a program drives a
coding agent: open a session in a workspace, send a prompt, follow what the agent does, answer
its permission requests, cancel it. It is JSON-RPC 2.0 over the agent's standard input and
output, one message per line. `qagents.integrations.acp.ACPAgent` is a generic ACP v1 client:
any agent that speaks ACP v1 becomes a qagents [external agent](../concepts/external-agents.md).

ACP drives an agent; MCP gives an agent tools. `ACPAgent` does the first. Its `mcp_servers=`
option does the second: it hands the agent MCP servers to mount in each session, for example
[qagents tools served over MCP](mcp-server.md).

`ACPAgent` needs no extra dependency: `pip install "qagents[acp]"` is an empty extra. Serving
qagents tools to the agent with `tool_server` needs `pip install "qagents[mcp]"`.

!!! note "Verified with Devvi only"
    `ACPAgent` is tested against Devvi's recorded ACP transcripts (`devvi --profile acp`).
    Other ACP agents are expected to work, but none has a recorded fixture yet. Record one
    before you rely on an agent ([below](#adding-a-recorded-fixture-for-a-new-agent)). For
    Devvi itself, use [`DevviAgent`](devvi.md), which adds Devvi's launcher, home, patch and
    environment rules on top of this client.

## Quick start

```python
from qagents import Agent, Permissions
from qagents.integrations.acp import ACPAgent

coder = ACPAgent(
    ["node", "C:/tools/some-agent/bin.js", "--acp"],  # a list, never a shell string
    name="coder",
    workspace="C:/work/repo",
    env={"SOME_SETTING": "1"},  # set for the agent process
    passthrough=["SOME_API_KEY"],  # copied from this process's environment, by name
    allow_unmetered=True,  # ACP reports no token counts
)
lead = Agent(
    "qcloud:<model-id>",
    tools=[coder.as_tool(timeout=1800)],
    permissions=Permissions(
        allow=["coder.read"],
        ask=["coder.edit", "coder.execute"],  # without an on_ask, "ask" is refused
    ),
)

async with coder:
    result = await lead.run("Make the failing test pass.")
```

Rules are checked in a fixed order: deny, `can_use_tool`, ask, allow, then the mode. An ask rule
therefore wins over an allow rule: `allow=["coder.read"], ask=["coder.*"]` asks about
`coder.read` too, and with no `on_ask` refuses it. Keep allow and ask patterns apart, as above,
or put the default in the mode. The lead's rules also decide the lead's own tool calls, the
call to `coder` included, so `mode="ask_all"` needs that tool in the allow list:
`Permissions(allow=["coder", "coder.read"], mode="ask_all")` runs `coder`, allows
`coder.read`, and asks about every other request of the agent. The names come from the agent's
tool calls ([Tool names for permission rules](#tool-names-for-permission-rules)), and the agent
sends a request only for the calls it chooses to ask about.

On Windows a `.js` agent runs as `["node", ".../bin.js"]`: Windows cannot execute a `.js` file,
and qagents never starts a `.cmd` or `.bat` shim (it would run through `cmd.exe`). A command
that names a `.js` file is refused with `... Windows starts only .exe and .com programs. Run it
with its interpreter, for example ['node', ...]`, and a path that does not exist with
`Cannot start '<path>': no such file.` A bare program name is looked up only in the absolute
`PATH` entries, never in the current directory.

## What the client does

1. **Starts the process** with `command`, in `cwd` (default: the workspace), with an explicit
   environment: the operating-system basics (`PATH`, `SYSTEMROOT`, `TEMP`, `TMP`,
   `USERPROFILE`, `HOME`, `LANG`, and on Windows `PATHEXT`, `COMSPEC`, `WINDIR`,
   `SYSTEMDRIVE`), plus `env=`, plus the `passthrough=` names. Nothing else of qagents'
   environment reaches the agent unless you pass `inherit_env=True`.
2. **`initialize`** with `protocolVersion: 1`, `clientInfo: {name: "qagents", version}` and
   client capabilities that offer nothing:

    ```json
    {"fs": {"readTextFile": false, "writeTextFile": false}, "terminal": false}
    ```

    The agent reads files and runs commands with its own tools, under its own sandbox, and asks
    qagents for permission. An agent that answers another protocol version is refused. Requests
    the agent sends that qagents does not implement (`fs/*`, `terminal/*`) are answered
    JSON-RPC -32601, so richer agents work too.
3. **`authenticate`**, only when the agent lists `authMethods` and you chose one with
   `auth_method=`. Without a choice qagents never starts a login. A method of type `terminal`
   (interactive) is refused: log in to the agent yourself first. If the agent then refuses
   `session/new` with "authentication required", the error lists the methods it offers.
4. **`session/new {cwd, mcpServers}`** for a new conversation. `cwd` is the absolute workspace;
   a turn without one is refused. A session this connection opened is continued directly while
   it is still open; an older or closed one with `session/resume`, or `session/load` (its
   replayed history is ignored) when the agent offers only that. MCP servers are sent again on
   every resume, because agents do not keep them.
5. **`session/set_config_option`** for `model=` and `config_options=`, when the session offers
   that option and its current value differs.
6. **`session/prompt`**. `session/update` notifications become qagents events;
   `session/request_permission` is answered by the permission bridge; the `stopReason` becomes
   the result's status.
7. **Cancel**: `session/cancel`, then `cancel_grace_s` seconds (default 5) for the agent to answer
   `stopReason: "cancelled"`; after that the process tree is killed and the next turn starts a
   new process. A cancel that comes before `session/prompt` is sent ends the turn at once,
   without sending it and without `session/cancel`: a setup request still waiting for its
   answer (`session/new`, `session/resume`, `session/load`, `session/set_config_option`) is
   given up, which the agent is told with `$/cancel_request`, and the process is kept.
8. **`session/close`** after a turn, for the idle sessions beyond `keep_sessions` (default 1),
   least recently used first, when the agent advertises `sessionCapabilities.close` and can
   resume or load sessions. The agent then releases what it holds for each one (Devvi: an agent
   in memory and a process per stdio MCP server). A later turn in such a session resumes it
   (step 4). The close runs in the background: the turn's result does not wait for it, and the
   next turn waits for it (up to 10 seconds) before it opens a session. A later turn in that
   session waits for the agent's answer (up to `request_timeout_s`), since an agent refuses to
   resume a session it is still closing; after that it ends `error` ("the agent is still
   closing it"). A failed close is logged; a later turn in that session tries
   `session/resume`, and if the agent refuses it, prompts the session directly.

One process serves many sessions, one prompt at a time per session. qagents also runs one turn
at a time per workspace. Only the `keep_sessions` most recently used idle sessions stay open,
so with the default, continuing an older session costs a `session/resume`. Raise
`keep_sessions` for an agent that is slow to resume; `0` closes every session after its turn.
An agent that cannot close and resume sessions keeps them all open until the agent is closed.

## Updates and events

| ACP `sessionUpdate` | qagents |
|---|---|
| `agent_message_chunk`, text | `text_delta` (a whole block for Devvi, a token chunk for agents that stream); a chunk with a new `messageId`, and each of Devvi's blocks, starts after a blank line |
| `agent_message_chunk`, other content | `external_event` `image`, `audio`, `resource_link`, ...; bytes are never forwarded |
| `agent_thought_chunk` | `reasoning_delta` |
| `tool_call` | `tool_call_started`, named `<prefix>.<tool>`; counts toward `max_external_turns` |
| `tool_call_update` | new input: `external_event` `tool_arguments`; a later `name` or `kind` (for Devvi, `title`) renames the call for the permission requests that follow and in `ExternalResult.tool_calls`; `completed` or `failed`: `tool_call_finished` |
| `usage_update {used, size}` | `external_event` `context`: context pressure, not token usage |
| `config_option_update` | `external_event` `config` |
| `plan` | `external_event` `plan` |
| anything else | `external_event` `unknown` with `raw_events=True`; otherwise counted in `ExternalResult.raw["ignored_events"]` |

| `stopReason` | status | `stop_reason` |
|---|---|---|
| `end_turn` | `completed` | `end_turn` |
| `max_tokens` | `limit_reached` | `max_tokens` |
| `max_turn_requests` | `limit_reached` | `max_turn_requests` |
| `refusal` | `completed` | `content_filter`; through `as_tool()` an error result |
| `cancelled` | `cancelled` | `cancelled` |
| another value | `completed` | the value (logged as a warning) |
| JSON-RPC -32603 `"Internal error: turn failed: X"` | `error` | `turn failed: X` |

`ExternalResult.raw["acp_stop_reason"]` keeps the raw `stopReason`. `ExternalResult.backend` is
`acp:<agentInfo.name>@<agentInfo.version>`.

## Tool names for permission rules

Every permission request is decided by your `Permissions` on `"<prefix>.<tool>"`, where the
prefix is the tool name the calling model sees. ACP gives a tool call a `title` for display, an
optional `name`, and a `kind` (`read`, `edit`, `execute`, ...).

The tool name is the tool call's `name`, else its `kind` (`execute`, `edit`, ...), else
`"unknown"`, from everything the agent said about the call before it asked (a
`tool_call_update` that adds a `kind` counts). This is `default_tool_name`. The `title` is
not used: most agents build it from the tool's input (`"make"`, `"setup.py"`, `"Run ls -la"`),
so the model would choose the name your rules match, and a title such as `"rm"` would get past
`deny=["coder.execute"]`. So write rules on kinds, as in the [quick start](#quick-start):
`coder.read`, `coder.edit`, `coder.execute`. A rule on a title, such as `deny=["coder.rm"]`,
never matches.

Devvi is the exception: its code sets the title to the tool's name (`bash`,
`mcp__db__query`), and its `kind` is always `other`. For Devvi (`agentInfo.name`
`deepseek-harness-acp`, listed in `TITLES_ARE_TOOL_NAMES`) qagents uses `title_tool_name`
instead: the `name`, else the title when it looks like a tool name, else the kind. Pass
`tool_name=title_tool_name` for another agent whose code does the same, or your own function
of the tool call's fields that returns a name:

```python
from qagents.integrations.acp import ACPAgent, title_tool_name

coder = ACPAgent(
    ["node", "C:/tools/some-agent/bin.js", "--acp"],
    name="coder",
    workspace="C:/work/repo",
    tool_name=title_tool_name,  # only for an agent whose code puts tool names in titles
)
```

## Permission answers

A request names its tool call (`toolCall.toolCallId`) and may describe it (`title`, `kind`,
`rawInput`). Devvi sends only the id, after the matching `tool_call` update with the title and
the arguments. qagents decides on the call's latest known fields and arguments, and starts the
call from the request when the request is the first to describe it. It answers:

| qagents decision | Answer |
|---|---|
| allow | `{"outcome": "selected", "optionId": <the first allow_once option>}` |
| deny | `{"outcome": "selected", "optionId": <the first reject_once option, else reject_always>}` |
| cancel (an error, a timeout, arguments that are not a JSON object, a turn being cancelled, even when the decision came in at that moment, a posture that defers) | `{"outcome": "cancelled"}` |

An `allow_always` option is never chosen: when the agent offers no `allow_once`, an allow is
answered "cancelled". A request without a tool call id, or for a session where no turn runs, is
answered "cancelled". As soon as the turn is cancelled, every pending request is answered
"cancelled". Who decides, in what order, and the postures, are in
[External agents](../concepts/external-agents.md#permission-requests).

## No token counts

ACP carries no token usage, only context pressure. (ACP also has an unstable `usage` field
with token counts; qagents does not read it yet.) `capabilities().token_usage` is `False`, so a
calling run with `max_total_tokens` or `max_cost_usd` refuses the agent at its first call,
unless you build it with `allow_unmetered=True` and accept that its spend is not counted. The
refusal comes after the handshake: the agent process is started, answers `initialize` and stays
up, but no session is opened and no prompt is sent.

## Crash safety

The agent chooses session ids, so a crash of the calling run between `session/new` and the
journaled result would lose the link. With `resumable=True` (only for agents that support
`session/resume` or `session/load`), the turn journals the session id as soon as it is known,
and journals that the prompt was sent before sending it. A call repeated after the crash then
resumes that session instead of opening a new one, and the tool is declared idempotent:

- the prompt had not been sent: the task is sent as usual;
- the prompt had been sent: the agent receives `EXTERNAL_AGENT_RESUME` ("The previous attempt was
  interrupted. Check the workspace state and finish the task.") followed by the task;
- the agent cannot reopen the session: the turn ends `interrupted` and is not started over.

Without `resumable=True` (the default) a repeated call is not made: the calling model is told
the outcome is unknown.

## MCP servers for the agent

```python
import sys

from qagents.integrations.acp import ACPAgent, MCPServerHTTP, MCPServerStdio

tickets = MCPServerStdio(
    "tickets",
    command=sys.executable,  # absolute: the agent starts it from its own directory
    args=["-m", "my_app.ticket_server"],
    passthrough=["TICKETS_TOKEN"],  # copied from this process's environment when a session opens
)
docs = MCPServerHTTP(
    "docs", url="http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer ..."}
)

coder = ACPAgent(
    ["node", "C:/tools/some-agent/bin.js", "--acp"],
    name="coder",
    workspace="C:/work/repo",
    mcp_servers=[tickets, docs],
)
```

- `MCPServerStdio(name, command, args=(), env={}, passthrough=())`: a server the agent starts
  for each session. `command` must be an absolute path. Values of `env` are never shown in
  `repr`. Name credentials explicitly: an agent may strip variables that look like secrets from
  what it passes on (Devvi does).
- `MCPServerHTTP(name, url, headers={})`: a server the agent reaches over Streamable HTTP.
  Needs an agent that advertises `mcpCapabilities.http`; otherwise the handshake fails with a
  configuration error. Header values are never shown in `repr`.
- A plain mapping is sent as it is (an ACP `McpServer` object).
- `mcp_servers=` can be a function of the turn. It runs only when servers are sent: when
  the turn opens a session (`session/new`) or reopens one (`session/resume`,
  `session/load`). A session this connection already has open is continued with the
  servers it has, and the function does not run.
    - Return the list (or an awaitable of it) for servers that live as long as the session.
    - Return an async context manager that yields the list for servers that live for one
      turn, such as a qagents tool server bound to the calling run. qagents enters it before
      the session opens, closes the session right after the turn (`session/close`), then
      exits it, so the next turn resumes the session with servers of its own. An agent that
      cannot close sessions keeps the session open, but it is not continued directly again: a
      later turn resumes it, or says why it cannot.

For example, a qagents tool server that lives for one turn and is bound to the calling run
([Serving tools over MCP](mcp-server.md#bound-to-a-run)):

```python
import contextlib

from qagents.integrations.acp import ACPAgent
from qagents.integrations.mcp_server import tool_server


def lookup_customer(email: str) -> str:
    """Find a customer by email."""
    return "Maria"


@contextlib.asynccontextmanager
async def turn_tools(turn):
    async with tool_server([lookup_customer], ctx=turn.parent) as server:
        yield [server.acp_config()]


coder = ACPAgent(
    ["node", "C:/tools/some-agent/bin.js", "--acp"],
    name="coder",
    workspace="C:/work/repo",
    mcp_servers=turn_tools,
)
```

`DevviAgent(expose_tools=...)` does the same for Devvi.

## Options

`ACPAgent(command, *, ...)`:

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `command` | required | program and arguments, as a list |
| `name` | `"acp"` | the agent's name; the default tool name and permission prefix |
| `env` | `{}` | variables set for the agent process |
| `passthrough` | `()` | names copied from qagents' environment, such as `["SOME_API_KEY"]` |
| `inherit_env` | `False` | give the agent qagents' whole environment, every secret in it too |
| `cwd` | the workspace | working directory of the agent process |
| `workspace` | `cwd` | the default `cwd` of sessions |
| `mcp_servers` | `()` | MCP servers to mount in each session, or a function of the turn |
| `model` | `None` | the model to select: an option value, an option name (`"deepseek-v4-pro"`), or, for agents whose values are JSON lists (Devvi), the list as a tuple; a model the session does not offer is refused |
| `config_options` | `{}` | other options, `{config id: value}`, for example `{"reasoning_effort": "high"}` |
| `auth_method` | `None` | the `authMethods` id to authenticate with; `None`: never authenticate |
| `resumable` | `False` | re-attach a call repeated after a crash (see above) |
| `raw_events` | `False` | forward unmapped `session/update` kinds as `external_event` `unknown` |
| `tool_name` | `default_tool_name` (`title_tool_name` for Devvi) | `(tool call fields) -> name`; see [Tool names for permission rules](#tool-names-for-permission-rules) |
| `keep_sessions` | 1 | sessions kept open after their turn; older idle ones are closed with `session/close` (when the agent can close and resume sessions), and a later turn in one resumes it; `0` closes each session after its turn |
| `handshake_timeout_s` | 60 | seconds for `initialize` and `authenticate` |
| `request_timeout_s` | 120 | seconds for `session/new`, `session/resume`, `session/load`, `session/set_config_option`; the prompt itself has no timeout (use `as_tool(timeout=...)` or the calling run's limits); also how long a turn waits for the `session/close` of the session it continues; a request without an answer ends the turn as `error` |
| `close_grace_s` | 5 | seconds the process gets to exit after its stdin closes, before its tree is killed |
| `max_line_bytes` | 32 MiB | largest message accepted from the agent |

Plus the `ExternalAgent` options: `description`, `permissions`, `on_permission`,
`approval_timeout_s`, `cancel_grace_s`, `max_external_turns`, `allow_unmetered`,
`track_changes`.

After the handshake, `agent.agent_info`, `agent.agent_capabilities`, `agent.auth_methods` and
`agent.session_config(session_id)` show what the agent reported.

## Errors

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| the program is missing, a `.cmd` shim on Windows, the handshake is refused or times out, another protocol version, a requested capability is missing, authentication fails | `ExternalAgentConfigurationError` when the agent connects; through `as_tool()` the model reads `... is unavailable` and later calls in the run fail at once |
| `session/new` answered -32602, -32600 or -32601 (an MCP server did not start, a refused `cwd`) | `ExternalAgentConfigurationError` |
| a model or option the session does not offer | `ExternalAgentConfigurationError`, listing what it offers |
| the turn failed (-32603) | status `error` with the agent's message; through `as_tool()` an error result the model can read |
| the error text says authentication, billing or a missing credential | status `error`, and the calling run stops calling the agent (`EXTERNAL_AGENT_UNAVAILABLE`) |
| the process exited, the stream ended or a pipe broke before `session/prompt` was sent, or a setup request got no answer | status `error` with the reason (nothing of the task reached the agent); `interrupted` and `raw["ambiguous"] = True` for a call repeated after a crash; the next turn starts a new process |
| the process exited, the stream ended or a pipe broke after `session/prompt` was sent | status `interrupted`, `raw["ambiguous"] = True`, the stderr tail in `raw["stderr_tail"]`; the next turn starts a new process |
| a cancel while the session is set up | status `cancelled`; the pending request is given up with `$/cancel_request`; the process is kept |
| a line over `max_line_bytes`, or three malformed lines in a row | the connection is closed: `interrupted` |
| the session to continue cannot be reopened | status `error`: `cannot continue session ...` |

## Adding a recorded fixture for a new agent

The offline tests drive `ACPAgent` against `tests/integrations/fakes/fake_acp_agent.py`, a
standard-library script that replays a recorded transcript as a real process. To add an agent,
do four things.

**Record its side of the wire.** Run the agent with a small task and save every line it writes
on stdout: the `initialize` result, the `session/new` result, the `session/update`
notifications, any `session/request_permission`, and the `session/prompt` result. Replace
volatile values with the placeholders the fake understands: `{{sessionId}}`, `{{messageId}}`,
`{{cwd}}`. Devvi's fixtures in `tests/fixtures/devvi/acp/` were made this way from Devvi's own
snapshots.

**Write the client side as directives** between the recorded lines. The fixture is JSON Lines,
and each line is one of:

| Line | Does |
|---|---|
| a JSON-RPC message (has `"jsonrpc"`) | written as recorded, after the placeholders are replaced; a response gets the id of the client request it answers |
| `{"expect": {"id", "method", "params"}}` | reads the next client message and checks the method and the given params (a subset); patterns `"$any"`, `"$absent"`, `"$absolute"`, `"$list"`, `"$string"` |
| `{"answer": {"id", "accept": [...]}, "otherwise": FILE}` | waits for the client's answer to the agent's request `id`; a different answer continues in `FILE` (a branch, such as the rejected recording) |
| `{"raw": TEXT}`, `{"big_chunk": N}`, `{"sleep": S}`, `{"exit": CODE, "stderr": TEXT}`, `{"hang": true}`, `{"write_file": {"path", "text"}}` | a malformed line, a large message, a pause, a crash, an agent that stops answering, an edit in the workspace |
| `{"fixture": ...}`, `{"comment": ...}` | nothing (a header or a note) |

A mismatch is written to stderr and ends the fake with exit code 3, so the test sees the
connection break and why.

**Test it** like the existing ones:

```python
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from qagents.integrations.acp import ACPAgent

FAKE = Path("tests/integrations/fakes/fake_acp_agent.py").resolve()
FIXTURE = Path("tests/fixtures/other-agent/acp/text-turn.jsonl").resolve()


async def test_other_agent_text_turn(tmp_path):
    agent = ACPAgent(
        [sys.executable, "-I", str(FAKE), "--script", str(FIXTURE)],
        name="other",
        workspace=tmp_path,
    )
    async with agent:
        result = await agent.run("Say hello")
    assert result.status == "completed"
    assert result.backend.startswith("acp:")
```

**Keep the agent's license notice** next to its fixtures, as `tests/fixtures/devvi/LICENSE` does
for Devvi's, and say in the docs which version of the agent the recording comes from.

Options of the fake that help: `--log FILE` (every client message, one JSON line each),
`--hang-after-cancel` (an agent that does not stop), `--child HEARTBEAT` (a child process, to
check that the whole tree is killed).

## Not in this version

- ACP's unstable `usage` field (token counts) is not read, so an ACP agent is unmetered.
- The `fs/*` and `terminal/*` client capabilities: qagents offers neither, and answers such
  requests JSON-RPC -32601.
- qagents as an ACP agent server, so that ACP clients could drive a qagents agent.
- Authentication is never automatic: qagents authenticates only with the `auth_method` you
  choose, and never with an interactive (`terminal`) method.

---

<!-- page: integrations/mcp-server.md | integrations/mcp-server/ -->

# Serving tools over MCP

A coding agent runs its own loop with its own tools. To let it use qagents tools as well, a
customer lookup or a ticket system, serve them to it over MCP.
`qagents.integrations.mcp_server` does that.

MCP gives an agent tools; it does not drive the agent. qagents drives agents over ACP or the
Devvi SDK ([External agents](../concepts/external-agents.md)), and serves them tools over MCP.
In this direction the coding agent is the MCP client and qagents is the server.

It needs the MCP Python SDK: `pip install "qagents[mcp]"`.

| Mode | Where the tools run | Who decides each call | Journal | Use it for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Bound to a run](#bound-to-a-run) (HTTP) | in your process | the run's `Permissions`, with its `on_ask` | the run's session | tools of a qagents run that drives the agent; the default |
| [On its own](#on-its-own) (HTTP) | in your process | the server's `permissions=` | none | a server outside any run |
| [stdio](#over-stdio-in-a-separate-process) | in a process the agent starts | the spec's rules; "ask" is refused | none | importable tools, any MCP client |

With Devvi you rarely call this module yourself: `DevviAgent(expose_tools=[...])` starts the
right server for every turn ([qagents tools inside Devvi](devvi.md#qagents-tools-inside-devvi)).

## Bound to a run

`tool_server(tools, ctx=ctx)` inside a running tool call binds the server to that call's run.
Every call that arrives over MCP is then an ordinary tool call of that run, made with
`RunContext.call_tool`:

- the run's `Permissions` decide it, with the run's `on_ask`. "Ask" without an `on_ask` is
  refused, because a call over MCP cannot pause the run. An approval with edited arguments is
  checked again and runs with the new arguments;
- it is journaled in the run's session before and after it runs (`approval_decided`,
  `tool_started`, `tool_result`), and counts toward `Limits.max_tool_calls` from before it is
  decided: calls that arrive together never pass the limit, and a refused call does not count;
- `Limits.parallel_tools` applies among the calls served through the same calling tool call: one
  that must run alone waits for the others from that caller. Calls served through different
  calling calls, and the model's own calls, are not kept apart from it. A call that runs alone
  also waits, within its own timeout, for the thread of an earlier sync call (served or the
  run's own, from anywhere in the run) that timed out and still runs. If that thread is still
  busy then, the call is not run (`TOOL_WAITED_FOR_EARLIER`);
- the run's `before_tool` and `after_tool` hooks see it (a hook that raises fails the run, as
  for the model's calls), and its `tool_call_started` and `tool_call_finished` events reach
  the run's stream;
- the tool gets the run's `deps` and `ctx.state`, and its usage is added to the run;
- its `ctx.operation_id` is `<calling call's operation id>:<call id>`, stable for the call;
- it runs one level below the calling tool call (`ctx.depth + 1`), because it comes from the
  agent that the tool call runs. An agent or external agent among the served tools therefore
  starts at `ctx.depth + 2`, and `Limits.max_depth` bounds chains through served tools as it
  bounds sub-agents.

So a qagents tool never runs without a qagents decision.

```python
from qagents import RunContext, tool
from qagents.integrations.acp import ACPAgent
from qagents.integrations.mcp_server import tool_server


@tool
async def coder(ctx: RunContext, task: str) -> str:
    """Delegate a coding task. The coding agent can look up customers and create tickets."""
    async with tool_server([lookup_customer, create_ticket], ctx=ctx) as server:
        agent = ACPAgent(
            ["node", "C:/tools/some-agent/bin.js", "--acp"],
            name="coder",
            workspace="C:/work/repo",
            mcp_servers=[server.acp_config()],  # an ACP session/new mcpServers entry
            allow_unmetered=True,
        )
        async with agent:
            result = await agent.run(task, parent=ctx)
    return result.for_model("coder")
```

This starts the agent for each call, with the server of that call. For Devvi,
`expose_tools` does the same with one long-lived process per workspace.

The journal entries of a served call carry `source: "mcp"`, `server` (the server name) and
`caller_tool_call_id` (the id of the tool call the server is bound to). Served call ids start
with `mcp-`.

| Entry | Written |
|---|---|
| `approval_decided` | when `on_ask` answered, before the call runs |
| `tool_started` | before the tool runs |
| `tool_result` | after it, with the result text and its usage |

The server refuses calls once the tool call it is bound to has ended, and journals nothing for
them. A call that was already journaled as started (it waited in `before_tool`, for example) is
checked again right before the tool runs: it then records the same refusal and does not run.
Start the server inside the tool, and close it before the tool returns.

## On its own

Without `ctx` the server decides calls with its own rules and journals nothing:

```python
from qagents import Limits, Permissions
from qagents.integrations.mcp_server import tool_server

rules = Permissions(allow=["lookup_customer"], deny=["delete_*"])
limits = Limits(tool_timeout_s=30)
async with tool_server([lookup_customer], permissions=rules, limits=limits) as server:
    url, headers = server.url, server.headers  # give both to the agent; never log the headers
    await run_agent_that_speaks_mcp(url, headers)
```

`permissions=` defaults to `Permissions()`: tools declared `requires_approval` are refused unless
an allow rule or an `on_ask` lets them run. `deps=` sets `ctx.deps` for the tools. Of `limits=`,
`tool_timeout_s`, `max_tool_result_chars`, `max_tool_calls`, `parallel_tools` and
`max_parallel_tools` apply.

`tool_server(tools, *, ctx=None, permissions=None, deps=None, limits=None, name="qagents",
approval_timeout_s=60.0, shutdown_timeout_s=10.0)` returns a `ToolServer`, not started yet; use it
with `async with`, or call `start()` and `aclose()`. `tools` takes what `Agent(tools=...)` takes:
tools, functions, agents, toolkits and lists of them. Two tools with the same name, and deferred
tools (their result would come from `agent.resume`, which an MCP caller cannot wait for), are
refused when the server starts. `ctx` together with `permissions`, `deps` or `limits` is refused:
a bound server uses the run's.

While it runs:

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| `server.url` | `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp` |
| `server.headers` | `{"Authorization": "Bearer <token>"}`: pass it only to the agent that should call the tools; never log it |
| `server.acp_config(name=None)` | `{"type": "http", "name", "url", "headers": [{"name", "value"}]}`, an ACP `session/new` `mcpServers` entry |
| `server.port`, `server.tools`, `server.bound`, `server.running` | the port, the served tools, whether it is bound, whether it serves |

## Over stdio, in a separate process

`python -I -m qagents.integrations.mcp_server --spec FILE` serves the tools a JSON spec lists, on
its standard input and output, until its input closes. The agent starts this process itself, so
the tools must be importable: there is no parent run here, the spec's rules decide, "ask" is
refused, and nothing is journaled.

```json
{
  "name": "qagents",
  "tools": ["my_app.tools:lookup_customer", "my_app.tools:TICKET_TOOLS"],
  "permissions": {"allow": ["create_ticket"], "deny": ["delete_*"]},
  "deps": "my_app.tools:make_deps"
}
```

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `"qagents"` | the MCP server name the agent sees |
| `tools` | required | `"package.module:attr"` references: a tool, a function, an agent, a toolkit, or a list of them |
| `permissions` | `{}` | `mode`, `allow`, `ask`, `deny`, as in `Permissions`, without callbacks |
| `paths` | `[]` | absolute directories put first on `sys.path` before the tools are imported |
| `deps` | `null` | `"package.module:attr"` of `ctx.deps`: a value, or a function (sync or async) called once, with no arguments, when the server starts |
| `tool_timeout_s` | 120 | seconds per call |
| `max_tool_result_chars` | 60000 | longer results are cut |
| `max_tool_calls` | `null` | calls the server runs before it refuses more, for the process's lifetime |

The process runs with `-I`: no current directory, no `PYTHONPATH` and no user site-packages on
`sys.path`. Install the tools' package in the environment, or list its directory in `paths`.

Build the spec and the command in code:

```python
from qagents.integrations.mcp_server import (
    ToolRules,
    ToolServerSpec,
    acp_stdio_config,
    stdio_command,
    tool_reference,
)

spec = ToolServerSpec(
    name="qagents",
    tools=[tool_reference(lookup_customer), "my_app.tools:TICKET_TOOLS"],
    permissions=ToolRules(allow=["create_ticket"], deny=["delete_*"]),
)
path = spec.write("C:/work/qagents-tools.json")  # the absolute path
command = stdio_command(path)  # [python, "-I", "-m", "qagents.integrations.mcp_server", ...]
entry = acp_stdio_config(path, name="qagents")  # an ACP session/new mcpServers entry
```

`tool_reference(tool)` gives `"module:attr"` for a tool defined at module level, and refuses one
defined in a function or in `__main__`, which another process cannot import. `stdio_command`
uses this interpreter's path made absolute but not resolved, so a virtual environment keeps its
packages. Put no secret in `acp_stdio_config(env=...)`: the agent may log its configuration.
Do not count on the server's environment either. The agent starts the server, and an agent may
drop every variable whose name looks like a credential before it does: Devvi removes names
matching `KEY|PASSWORD|SECRET|TOKEN` and names starting with `DSH_`
(`packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/index.ts` in the Devvi repository). Tools that need a credential
load it in a `deps` factory (the spec's `deps`) that reads a file or a credential store, for
example:

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path


def make_deps() -> dict:
    """The spec's "deps": "my_app.tools:make_deps". Called once, when the server starts."""
    path = Path.home() / ".my_app" / "tickets.json"  # not in the agent's workspace
    return {"tickets_token": json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["token"]}
```

A tool then reads `ctx.deps["tickets_token"]`. `Path.home()` works in the server's scrubbed
environment, since `USERPROFILE` and `HOME` are kept. A file is not hidden from the agent:
Devvi's sandbox does not confine reads on Windows, so the agent's own tools could read it too.
Where that matters, read the credential from the operating system's credential store instead.

Any MCP client can start it. For example, in a client configuration file:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "qagents-tools": {
      "command": "C:\\work\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe",
      "args": ["-I", "-m", "qagents.integrations.mcp_server", "--spec", "C:\\work\\qagents-tools.json"]
    }
  }
}
```

To check a spec by hand:

```powershell
python -I -m qagents.integrations.mcp_server --spec C:\work\qagents-tools.json --log-level INFO
```

A bad spec, or a tool that cannot be served, exits at once with code 2 and the reason on
stderr. A good one waits for a client on its standard input (on Windows, `Ctrl+Z` then Enter
ends it). Exit codes: 0 when its input closed, 2 for a bad spec, 1 for any other failure. While it serves, stray output of the tools
(`print`) goes to stderr, not into the protocol stream.

## What the calling agent sees

Each tool's name, its description and the JSON Schema of its arguments, exactly as a qagents
model would see them, plus MCP annotations from the tool's flags: `readOnlyHint` for
`read_only`, `idempotentHint` for `idempotent`. A result is one text block, the text a qagents
model would read. Errors (invalid arguments, a `ToolError`, a timeout, a refusal) are MCP results
with `isError` set, so the calling agent's model can read them and adapt.

Refusals read `'create_ticket' was not run: <reason>`. The reasons are `TOOL_SERVER_*` strings,
in `qagents.prompts`:

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| the rule's own reason | a deny rule, `can_use_tool` (also when it raises), a declined approval |
| `it needs approval, and nobody can approve it while the calling agent waits.` | "ask" with no `on_ask` |
| `the approval did not arrive within 60 seconds.` | `on_ask` took longer than `approval_timeout_s` |
| `the qagents run that serves this tool is no longer running.` | a bound server whose tool call ended |
| `the qagents tool server is shutting down.` | a call during shutdown |

Every other text is the agent loop's own wording (`qagents.prompts`).

## Security

- The server listens on `127.0.0.1` only, on a random port. On Windows the port is bound with
  `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE`, so no other process can share it.
- Every request must carry the server's bearer token, a new random value per server, compared
  in constant time; anything else gets `401`. The token keeps out other local users and
  browser pages, not code that runs as your own user.
- DNS rebinding protection: the `Host` must be `127.0.0.1:<port>`, and a browser `Origin` must
  be `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`.
- At most 16 MCP sessions at a time; no websockets.
- Only `127.0.0.1` (IPv4). A client that resolves `localhost` to `::1` must use `server.url` as
  given.

## With Devvi

`DevviAgent(expose_tools=[...])` starts a bound server for every turn and passes it in the
session's `mcpServers`; Devvi shows the tools to its model as `mcp__qagents__<tool>`. Two gates
apply:

1. Devvi's own pipeline could ask permission for `mcp__qagents__<tool>`; with its default
   profile it asked nothing in tier 1. The bridge would decide such a request as
   `coder.mcp__qagents__<tool>`; with no rule it is refused.
2. The server decides the call itself with the lead's rules, on the tool's own name. This is
   the gate that always applies.

So `allow=["coder.mcp__qagents__*"]` at the bridge is safe; put the rules for each tool on its
qagents name. Devvi gives an MCP tool call 60 seconds
(`packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/index.ts` in the Devvi repository): keep the lead's
`Limits.tool_timeout_s` under a minute (an `on_ask` for an exposed tool is bounded by 50
seconds). If Devvi gives up first, it cancels the request, and the server records the call as
interrupted.

## With any MCP-capable agent

Give the agent `server.url` and `server.headers` (HTTP), or the stdio command. For an ACP agent,
pass `server.acp_config()` or `acp_stdio_config(path)` in `ACPAgent(mcp_servers=[...])`; MCP
servers are sent again on every session resume, because ACP agents do not keep them.

## Shutting down

Leaving `async with` (or `await server.aclose()`) refuses new calls, cancels running ones, ends
the MCP sessions and closes the port, within `shutdown_timeout_s`. `aclose()` is safe to cancel,
for example by a deadline around `async with`: the shutdown goes on in a task of its own and
still closes the port, and a second `aclose()` waits for it. A cancelled bound call records
`TOOL_INTERRUPTED` ("outcome unknown"), or `TOOL_CANCELLED` for a read-only tool: only a
read-only call is harmless when it is cut short.

!!! note "Not in this version"
    - Results are text only: structured content and images are not sent as MCP
      `structuredContent` or image blocks.
    - "Ask" cannot pause the parent run over MCP; it is refused unless an `on_ask` answers.

---

<!-- page: coding-agents.md | coding-agents/ -->

# Docs for coding agents

Coding agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, VS Code, any MCP client) write better qagents
code when they read the documentation of the version you have installed instead of guessing
from other frameworks. qagents gives them four ways in:

| Way | For | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| The **docs MCP server**, `python -m qagents.docs_mcp` | agents that speak MCP | `pip install "qagents[mcp]"` |
| The **command line**, `python -m qagents.docs_mcp search "..."` | agents with a shell but no MCP | qagents |
| **`llms.txt`** and **`llms-full.txt`** on the docs site | chat assistants and web tools | a browser |
| **`AGENTS.md`** and the **Claude Code skill** | rules the agent reads up front | a copy in your project (`python -m qagents.docs_mcp skill`) |

The server and the command line answer from the installed package: the API comes from the code
that will run, and the guides from the docs that ship with it. When a guide and the API
disagree, the API answer wins.

## What the server offers

Tools, all read-only:

| Tool | What it returns |
|---|---|
| `search_docs(query, limit)` | Ranked sections of the guides, the README, the examples and the API docstrings, each with a snippet and its source (`page.md#anchor` or `file:line`) |
| `read_page(path, section)` | A whole page or one section, with the API reference filled in from the installed package |
| `list_pages()` | The table of contents with a one-line summary per page, the version, and where the docs were read from |
| `get_api(symbol)` | Signature, docstring, members and source location of any public name, such as `Agent.run` or `qagents.toolkits.files` |
| `list_examples()`, `read_example(name)` | The examples gallery and the code of one example |
| `check_code(code)` | A static check of a snippet: imports, attributes and keyword arguments against the installed signatures, and coroutines that are not awaited, each with the closest real name |

Resources: `qagents://llms.txt`, `qagents://docs/{path}` (every page, and also `README.md`,
`AGENTS.md` and the skill, `skills/qagents/SKILL.md`) and `qagents://examples/{name}`. Prompts: `build_agent` (build a new agent the qagents way) and
`review_code` (review code against the installed API and the qagents principles; it includes
the `check_code` report).

Check that it works before you connect an agent:

```bash
pip install "qagents[mcp]"
python -m qagents.docs_mcp pages
```

## Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add qagents-docs -- python -m qagents.docs_mcp
```

Everything after `--` is the command Claude Code starts. Use the interpreter of the environment
where qagents is installed. On Windows with a virtual environment:

```powershell
claude mcp add qagents-docs -- C:\path\to\project\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m qagents.docs_mcp
```

`--scope project` (`-s project`) writes the server to `.mcp.json` in the project, so everyone
who clones it gets it; the default scope, `local`, is only for you in this project. The
project file looks like this:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "qagents-docs": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["-m", "qagents.docs_mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

**The skill.** `skills/qagents/SKILL.md` tells Claude Code when to use the server and gives it a
short cheat sheet. Write the copy of your installed version into your project:

```bash
python -m qagents.docs_mcp skill --to .claude/skills/qagents
```

Use `--to ~/.claude/skills/qagents` instead for all your projects. The command writes
`SKILL.md` into that folder as UTF-8, and does not replace a different `SKILL.md` there unless
you add `--force`. `python -m qagents.docs_mcp skill` prints the file instead (on Windows
PowerShell 5.1, `>` would save it as UTF-16, so prefer `--to`). Agents connected to the server
read it with `read_page("skills/qagents/SKILL.md")`. If your install has no copy, the command
says so; the skill is also in the qagents repository, in the
[`skills/qagents`](https://github.com/mpvasilis/qagents/tree/main/skills/qagents) folder.
Claude Code loads it whenever code imports qagents or you ask for a qagents agent.

## Codex CLI

```bash
codex mcp add qagents-docs -- python -m qagents.docs_mcp
```

Or add it to `~/.codex/config.toml` yourself:

```toml
[mcp_servers.qagents-docs]
command = "python"
args = ["-m", "qagents.docs_mcp"]
```

`codex mcp list` shows the configured servers. Codex reads the `AGENTS.md` of the repository
it works in, so in your own project it does not see the one in qagents. Give it the rules as
described in [AGENTS.md](#agentsmd) below.

## Cursor

Add the server to `.cursor/mcp.json` in your project (or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` for every
project):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "qagents-docs": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["-m", "qagents.docs_mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

The Cursor command line can also add it to your user profile:

```bash
cursor --add-mcp '{"name":"qagents-docs","command":"python","args":["-m","qagents.docs_mcp"]}'
```

## VS Code

GitHub Copilot's agent mode reads `.vscode/mcp.json` in the workspace. Note the top-level key
is `servers`:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "qagents-docs": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["-m", "qagents.docs_mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Or add it to your user profile from the command line:

```bash
code --add-mcp '{"name":"qagents-docs","command":"python","args":["-m","qagents.docs_mcp"]}'
```

## Any MCP client

The server speaks MCP over stdio. Configure the command `python` with the arguments
`-m qagents.docs_mcp`, using the Python of the environment where qagents is installed. It needs
no network access, no API key and no environment variables.

## Without MCP: the command line

Every tool has a command that prints the same Markdown:

```bash
python -m qagents.docs_mcp search "pause a tool call for approval"
python -m qagents.docs_mcp read concepts/permissions.md pause-and-resume
python -m qagents.docs_mcp pages
python -m qagents.docs_mcp api Agent.resume
python -m qagents.docs_mcp examples
python -m qagents.docs_mcp example supervisor
python -m qagents.docs_mcp check my_agent.py
python -m qagents.docs_mcp llms
python -m qagents.docs_mcp skill --to .claude/skills/qagents
```

`check` exits with status 1 when it finds problems, so it also works as a pre-commit step.
`qagents docs ...` (or `python -m qagents docs ...`) is the same command line under a shorter
name: `qagents docs search "pause a tool call for approval"`.
`search` takes `--limit N` and `--kind docs|example|api`.

## llms.txt

The published site serves [`llms.txt`](llms.txt), an index of every page with a one-line
description in the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format, and `llms-full.txt`, every page in
one file. Give either to a chat assistant that cannot run the server. They are written by
`scripts/build_llms_txt.py` from the same corpus the server reads, and MkDocs copies them from
`docs/` into the site.

## AGENTS.md

`AGENTS.md` at the root of the qagents repository has two parts. Part 1 has rules and patterns
for agents that write code with qagents (look names up, never invent them, mark side effects,
test with `ScriptedModel`). Part 2 has the layout, commands and principles for agents that work
on qagents itself.

Codex, Cursor and other tools read the `AGENTS.md` at the root of the repository they work in.
Inside a qagents checkout that is this file. In your own project that depends on qagents,
nothing reads it for you. Do one of these:

- Copy Part 1 of qagents' `AGENTS.md` into your project's `AGENTS.md` (create the file at your
  repository root if you have none). Codex and Cursor then read the rules on their own.
- Or tell the agent to read it from the docs server: `read_page("AGENTS.md")`, or
  `python -m qagents.docs_mcp read AGENTS.md` on the command line. The server has the copy of
  the installed version.

## Where the docs come from

The server uses the first of these that has a `docs` folder, and `list_pages()` says which:

1. `--docs-dir DIR`, when given: `python -m qagents.docs_mcp --docs-dir DIR`.
2. The copy bundled in the installed wheel.
3. The repository checkout, for an editable install (`pip install -e .`).
4. The `QAGENTS_DOCS_DIR` environment variable: a qagents checkout or its `docs` folder.

The API reference always comes from the installed package, so `get_api` and `check_code` are
right even when the guides come from another version (`list_pages()` then warns).

## MCP gives an agent tools; it does not drive one

MCP is how you give an agent tools and context, such as these docs: the agent is the client
and decides when to call the server.

MCP is a tool protocol. An agent that serves itself as an MCP tool (Codex:
`codex mcp-server`) can be called through `MCPToolkit`, but each turn is then one opaque call:
qagents cannot follow its steps, decide its permission requests one by one, or cancel it and
keep the session. To make a coding agent work for a qagents agent, drive it over ACP or the
Devvi SDK.

**ACP** is the Agent Client Protocol, which many coding agents speak; the **Devvi SDK** is
Devvi's own protocol. See [External agents](concepts/external-agents.md). The two directions
combine: a qagents agent drives a coding agent over ACP, and that coding agent reads these
docs over MCP.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| The client cannot start the server | Use the full path of the environment's Python, for example `.venv\Scripts\python.exe` on Windows |
| `needs the MCP Python SDK 2.x` | `pip install "qagents[mcp]"`; the command line works without it |
| `list_pages()` says "no docs folder" | Point `QAGENTS_DOCS_DIR` at a qagents checkout, or use `--docs-dir` |
| Answers mention another version | The guides come from another checkout; `get_api` still reads the installed code |

---

<!-- page: design.md | design/ -->

# Principles and guarantees

qagents was designed after a survey of the agent frameworks of late 2026
([research report, in Greek](research.md)). This page records the decisions that follow from it,
what the library guarantees, and what it deliberately leaves out.

## Principles

**The journal is the product; the loop is small.** Frameworks that froze something else first
(the conversation between agents, a graph runtime, one vendor's wire format) paid for it with
rewrites. The durable artefact here is the append-only session journal. Sessions, approvals,
resume, compaction and workflows are all views of it.

**Record first, act second.** A model response is written to the journal before any tool it
requested starts, and every tool start and result is written as it happens. After a failure the
journal says exactly how far the run got.

**Nothing hidden.** The framework sends your instructions, your messages and your tool
descriptions. The few strings it adds are in `qagents.prompts`. There are no default personas,
no hidden system prompts and no prompt templating language.

**Control lives in code, outside the model.** Permissions are deterministic rules evaluated in a
fixed order: the first rule that answers decides, `deny` is checked first and always wins, and
any failure while deciding refuses the call.
Hooks that raise stop the run. Published prompt-injection defences that rely on detection have
all been bypassed; rules and least privilege are what holds.

**Safe by default.** Runs have a turn limit. Tools that are not declared read-only run one at a
time. Tools with side effects ask first. Requests that may have been billed are not repeated.
Message content stays out of traces unless you ask for it.

**Fail early and say why.** A setting the provider would reject fails when the agent is built.
A model without the needed capability fails before the request is sent. Errors name what to do.

**Provider- and agent-neutral.** Models and agents sit behind thin adapters. Conversations are
stored as typed parts, not as one vendor's JSON, with opaque provider data kept for replay;
QCloud is the first-class provider, not the only one. Another agent program (Devvi, any ACP
agent) is an external agent behind one contract, `ExternalAgent`: qagents gives it a task,
decides its permission requests and keeps the journal, whichever agent it is. There is no
universal gateway dependency.

## Compared with what exists

| Documented gap elsewhere | What qagents does |
|---|---|
| Graph frameworks re-run the whole node after a crash or an approval, and match interrupts by position | Resume is per tool call, keyed by call id; a finished call never runs again |
| Checkpoints serialised with pickle | The journal is plain JSON |
| Prompts injected by the framework that the developer cannot see | One file of strings, all replaceable |
| No default limits on turns or spend | `max_turns=30` by default; token, cost and time limits available |
| Hooks or permission checks that fail open | A failing check refuses; a failing hook stops the run |
| Unknown request fields dropped silently, or rejected mid-run with a 400 | Checked against the provider's allow-list when the agent is built |
| Vendor SDKs tied to one model family or one API | Any provider behind one `stream` method; Chat Completions is first-class |
| Every pause and resume re-runs side effects | Recorded results are reused; `ctx.operation_id` gives tools a stable idempotency key |
| Coding agents wrapped as one opaque tool call, or "driven" over a tool protocol | External agents are driven over ACP or the Devvi SDK: every permission request goes through your rules, each step is an event, a cancel stops the turn and keeps the session |

## Guarantees

What you can rely on, and what you cannot.

| Guarantee | Scope |
|---|---|
| A tool call with a recorded result is never run again | per session journal |
| A model response is journaled before its tool calls start | always |
| An interrupted, non-idempotent tool call is not repeated; the model is told the outcome is unknown | on `resume` and on the next `run` |
| `ctx.operation_id` is identical when a call is repeated after a resume | per run |
| An ambiguous model request is not repeated | unless `Limits(retry_ambiguous=True)` |
| A denied or failed permission check never runs the tool | always |
| The conversation sent to the provider is always well-formed (every tool call has a result) | always |
| An external agent's permission request is decided by your rules, never answered "allow always", and refused when deciding fails: a `can_use_tool` or `on_ask` that raises answers reject, a decision that times out answers cancelled | always |

The guarantees for calls to external agents, including crash recovery, are listed in
[External agents](concepts/external-agents.md#guarantees-for-external-calls).

Not guaranteed:

- **Exactly-once side effects.** Delivery is at-least-once. Use `ctx.operation_id` with the
  system your tool calls.
- **Liveness.** Nothing detects a dead run and resumes it for you unless you run
  `AgentRuntime`, whose `recover()` resumes runs whose worker's lease expired.
- **Cost accuracy.** `cost_usd` is computed from catalog prices and reported tokens.
- **Model behaviour.** Whether a model calls tools reliably or honours a JSON schema depends on
  the model and how it is served. Measure it on the models you use.

## What is verified

| Area | How it was checked |
|---|---|
| Loop, tools, permissions, hooks, limits, cancel, structured output | unit tests with scripted models |
| Sessions, crash recovery, approvals, compaction, workflows | unit tests, including SQLite across store instances and tasks killed mid-tool |
| OpenAI-compatible provider | tests against a local HTTP transport: streaming, tool-call deltas, retries, error mapping |
| QCloud provider | tests through the real `qcloud_ai` 0.4.0 SDK with its HTTP transport replaced locally |
| Toolkits | unit tests, including path-escape and non-public-address refusals |
| Tracing | tests with the OpenTelemetry SDK's in-memory exporter |
| Examples and documentation | examples are executed, documentation code blocks are compiled |
| External agents: ACP client, Devvi (ACP and SDK transports), MCP tool server | offline tests against Devvi's recorded ACP and SDK transcripts, fake agent processes started as real subprocesses, process-tree kill on Windows, the official MCP client over stdio and Streamable HTTP; opt-in tests (`-m devvi_mock`) against the real Devvi 0.2.1-rc.3 CLI and a local mock model |
| Docs server for coding agents | tests of search ranking on known questions, sections, live API introspection, the code checker on correct and wrong code, the command line, and the MCP server over stdio with the official client |

Not verified yet:

- A request against the live QCloud API. `examples/live_acceptance.py` exists for this and has
  only been run with `--dry-run`.
- Tool-calling and structured-output reliability of specific catalog models.
- Python 3.11 and 3.12, Linux and macOS. The suite ran on Python 3.13 on Windows, where the
  POSIX file-symlink test of `file_tools` is skipped (the junction tests run).
- Behaviour under load and with long journals.
- External agents against a paid model route (Devvi tier 2), on Linux or macOS, or on Node 24.9
  or newer without the compatibility hook the tier-1 tests used on Node 22.17. Other ACP agents
  than Devvi have no recorded fixture yet.

## Deliberately left out

| Not included | Why |
|---|---|
| A graph DSL or Pregel-style runtime | Most flows are sequential; a superstep barrier ties parallel branches together. Workflows are plain Python. |
| Role-play crews, group chat, an LLM manager | Studies of multi-agent failures point at coordination, not model capability. One orchestrator with isolated workers is what holds up. |
| Built-in RAG, vector stores, a memory product | Retrieval is a tool you write; file-based notes are competitive with memory layers in published benchmarks. |
| A universal provider gateway | A compromised release of a popular gateway shipped a credential stealer in 2026, and gateways lose reasoning state. Thin adapters are less risk. |
| An in-process code sandbox | An in-process sandbox is not a security boundary. |
| Pickled state | Stored state is a trust boundary. |
| Driving agents over MCP | MCP is a tool protocol: one call, one result. A coding agent's turn has a session, many steps, permission requests back to the caller, and a cancel that keeps the session. Agents are driven over ACP (or the Devvi SDK); MCP only gives them tools. |

## Roadmap

Shipped in 0.2: `PostgresStore` and `AgentRuntime` with leases and a recovery worker that
resumes dead runs, the MCP client toolkit (spec revision 2026-07-28, with fallback to
2025-11-25), signed approvals, the final-answer tool as a third structured-output mode, limits
inherited by sub-agents, and the Anthropic Messages and AG-UI adapters. Since 0.2: external
agents (the ACP client, Devvi, the MCP tool server) and the docs server for coding agents.

Next, in this order:

1. **Live acceptance on QCloud**: the paid checks in `examples/live_acceptance.py`, with usage
   and cost reconciled, and a small tool-calling evaluation per model in use.
2. **Deferred tool loading** for large tool sets, and journal snapshots.
3. **External agents**: live Devvi acceptance (one paid task, usage reconciled), recorded
   fixtures for more ACP agents, the devvi.sh platform as a `Model`, and qagents as an ACP
   agent server.

## Stability

The project is 0.x: names can still change between minor versions. The session journal is the
part meant to freeze first. New entry kinds and new event types may be added; readers should
ignore kinds they do not know. The strings in `qagents.prompts` are part of the behaviour, so
changes to them will be listed in release notes.

---

<!-- page: research.md | research/ -->

# Τα agentic frameworks συγκλίνουν σε μικρό πυρήνα

!!! info "About this page"
    The research that informed the design of qagents, written in Greek in November 2026.
    Version numbers, download counts and vendor claims are as found on 10 November 2026.

Τον Νοέμβριο του 2026 τα agentic frameworks έχουν καταλήξει, από διαφορετικούς δρόμους, στην ίδια αρχιτεκτονική: έναν σταθερό loop μοντέλου και tools με λίγα σημεία επέκτασης, ένα «harness» έτοιμων δυνατοτήτων γύρω του, και γράφους ή workflows μόνο για τον ντετερμινιστικό έλεγχο γύρω από τον agent. **Κανένα δεν προσφέρει exactly-once εκτέλεση**: όλα αποθηκεύουν state στα όρια των βημάτων και ξανατρέχουν το βήμα που ήταν σε εξέλιξη, άρα τα side effects χρειάζονται idempotency keys από τον σχεδιασμό. Τα τεκμηριωμένα κενά επαναλαμβάνονται: το open-source LangGraph αποθηκεύει state αλλά δεν επανεκκινεί μόνο του νεκρά runs, το CrewAI στέλνει prompts που ο developer δεν βλέπει, το Claude Agent SDK μιλά μόνο με Claude, το OpenAI Agents SDK κρατά τα καλύτερα χαρακτηριστικά του πίσω από το Responses API, και τα περισσότερα άλλαξαν αρχιτεκτονική ή API μέσα στο 2026. Για ένα νέο Python framework με κύριο provider μια ιδιωτική πλατφόρμα που εκθέτει μόνο Chat Completions, η σύσταση είναι **ένας πυρήνας δέκα στοιχείων**: provider adapter με capability profile και allow-list παραμέτρων, canonical typed μηνύματα, tool registry, loop με ρητά όρια, ενιαίο event stream, append-only event log με κανόνα «πρώτα καταγραφή, μετά ενέργεια», ένα μοναδικό extension interface, structured output με επικύρωση, tracing και ένα ψεύτικο μοντέλο για tests. Το MCP, τα durable-execution backends, το compaction, οι subagents, τα workflows, το sandbox, το voice και οι adapters A2A και AG-UI γίνονται προαιρετικά plugins. Υποχρεωτικό graph DSL, role-play «crews», ενσωματωμένο RAG, κρυφά prompts και καθολικό gateway τύπου LiteLLM μένουν σκόπιμα εκτός. Το σενάριο real-time/voice είναι το πιο αδύναμα τεκμηριωμένο: η έρευνα δεν κάλυψε speech pipelines, οπότε εκεί η αναφορά δίνει σχεδιαστικές αρχές και όχι επιλογή τεχνολογίας.

## Έξι σχολές κατέληξαν στον ίδιο loop με hooks

Η αγορά δεν χωρίζεται πια σε «frameworks» αλλά σε στρώσεις: βιβλιοθήκη, runtime και harness, όπως το διατυπώνει η ίδια η LangChain τον Φεβρουάριο του 2026 ([LangChain](https://langchain.com/blog/on-agent-frameworks-and-agent-observability)). Τα έργα που εξετάστηκαν ανήκουν σε έξι σχολές: graph orchestration (LangGraph, LlamaIndex Workflows, Haystack, Mastra), role-based multi-agent (CrewAI, Agno, AutoGen και ο διάδοχός του), vendor harness SDKs (Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK, AWS Strands, Vercel AI SDK), ελαφριά typed frameworks (Pydantic AI, smolagents), prompt compilers (DSPy) και durable-execution μηχανές. Ο πίνακας δίνει την κατάσταση όπως μετρήθηκε στις 10 Νοεμβρίου 2026. Η στήλη «δυνατό σημείο» είναι εκτίμηση της έρευνας· η στήλη «τεκμηριωμένο κενό» στηρίζεται σε επίσημη τεκμηρίωση, release notes ή ανεξάρτητες δοκιμές.

| Έργο | Έκδοση, άδεια, γλώσσες | Κεντρική αρχιτεκτονική απόφαση | Δυνατό σημείο (εκτίμηση) | Τεκμηριωμένο κενό | Πηγές |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LangGraph / LangChain | `langgraph` 1.2.20 (5/11/2026), `langchain` 1.4.10 · MIT · Python, TypeScript | Pregel runtime με channels και reducers σε super-steps· `create_agent` ως σταθερός loop με έξι middleware hooks· Deep Agents ως harness | Checkpoint, interrupt και time travel ως ένας μηχανισμός· καλά ορισμένο merge στο parallel fan-in | Re-execution σε επίπεδο node· `interrupt()` με αντιστοίχιση κατά θέση· καμία αυτόματη ανάκτηση στο OSS· τρία stream formats ταυτόχρονα | [PyPI](https://pypi.org/pypi/langgraph/json), [Pregel docs](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/pregel), [interrupts](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/interrupts), [changelog](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/changelog-py) |
| CrewAI | 1.15.39 (9/11/2026) · MIT · Python | Crews (role, goal, backstory) για αυτονομία και Flows (`@start`, `@listen`, `@router`, `@persist`) για ντετερμινιστικό έλεγχο | Το ταχύτερο on-ramp της κατηγορίας· Crews ως βήματα μέσα σε Flows | Default prompts που ο developer δεν βλέπει, καταγεγραμμένα στην ίδια την τεκμηρίωση· αναξιόπιστο hierarchical process· LLM calls σε κάθε memory save | [releases](https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/releases), [flows](https://docs.crewai.com/en/concepts/flows.md), [prompts guide](https://docs.crewai.com/en/guides/advanced/customizing-prompts.md), [memory](https://docs.crewai.com/en/concepts/memory.md) |

| AutoGen και Semantic Kernel | AutoGen python-v0.7.5 (30/9/2025)· SK python-1.47.0 (5/11/2026) · MIT | AutoGen: actor-model Core και AgentChat από πάνω· SK: Kernel με plugins | Τα patterns (group chat, Magentic-One, handoff) πέρασαν στο MAF | Το README του AutoGen το δηλώνει archived και χωρίς συντήρηση· το SK χαρακτηρίζεται ως διάδοχη κατάσταση του MAF, με υποστήριξη τουλάχιστον έναν χρόνο μετά το GA | [AutoGen README](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/main/README.md), [SK README](https://github.com/microsoft/semantic-kernel/blob/main/README.md), [SK και MAF](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/agent-framework/semantic-kernel-and-microsoft-agent-framework/) |
| Agno | v3.1.12 (29/10/2026) · Apache-2.0 · Python | Agent, Team και Workflow, με το AgentOS ως FastAPI app που φιλοξενείς μόνος σου | Framework και self-hosted runtime ως ένα πακέτο· φθηνά stateless agent objects | Δύο breaking majors σε περίπου έναν χρόνο (το v3.0 απαιτεί database migration)· 1.908 open issues· marketing πάνω σε micro-benchmark instantiation | [GitHub](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno), [AgentOS](https://docs.agno.com/agent-os/overview), [v3.0.0](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/releases/tag/v3.0.0) |
| Claude Agent SDK | 0.2.180 (9/11/2026) · wrapper MIT, bundled binary υπό εμπορικούς όρους · Python, TypeScript | Thin client γύρω από το Claude Code binary: `query()` με options, ένα subprocess ανά session | Ολόκληρο production harness ως βιβλιοθήκη: permission pipeline, compaction, subagents, skills | Μόνο Claude· state σε τοπικό δίσκο· `max_turns` και `max_budget_usd` χωρίς default όριο· η Python υστερεί της TypeScript | [PyPI](https://pypi.org/pypi/claude-agent-sdk/json), [hosting](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting), [agent loop](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop), [gateway guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol) |
